title: Represent differential rungs with side-aware multiport scattering
description: Current coupled BKM exposes differential bottom/top rung ports only. TB303 resonance is single-ended from QL4.emitter back to QL1.emitter, so removing the synthetic feedback source makes resonance electrically present in coupling elements but not effective at the rung boundary. Implement side-aware multiport scattering or an equivalent differential-rung primitive so left/right emitter feedback paths participate without adding ideal source ports.
close_reason: Implemented side-aware differential rung BKM ports with bottom L/R side ports, top differential port, runtime scattering, and sparse Jacobian coverage.

title: Replace independent TB303 rung bias resistors with shared cutoff current
description: tb303_filter.pedal currently biases rungs independently with R_bias_floor/R_bias2/R_bias3/R_bias4, so cutoff mostly moves Q1 while Q2-Q4 keep fixed operating points. Model a single I_f/cutoff current source or expo-converter-equivalent that coherently sets all rung diode operating points, matching the real 303 cutoff contract.
close_reason: Implemented explicit TB303 cutoff converter boundary and shared ladder tail-current sink; focused cutoff/control tests are green.

title: Model TB303 filter as coupled differential ladder
description: Current tb303_filter.pedal topology is effectively four single-ended diode/RC stages chained emitter-to-base. Replace it with a coupled differential diode ladder structure: two diode chains, capacitors between corresponding ladder nodes, shared ladder current path, audio injected through the bottom differential pair/current modulation, and output taken from the correct ladder node. This should address the shallow BKM transition-band shape and move validation toward Stinchcombe H_tb/10-pole behavior without compiler hacks.

title: Remove VCC injection for single-NL WDF stages (BJT/DiodePair)
description:
VCC injection adds DC bias to reflected wave b1 AFTER tree processing, bypassing coupling caps. This causes DC offset accumulation through serial stage chain — Big Muff Q1 output has 0 zero crossings (entirely positive), killing AC signal for all downstream stages. Root cause of MUFF buzzing bug.

FIX:
1. build.rs:2442-2524 — Remove needs_vcc_bias for BjtNpn/BjtPnp/DiodePair/SingleDiode/Zener. Stop remapping VCC→GND for these types. Remove compute_vcc_injection_single() call.
2. build.rs:2574-2700 — Can remove compute_vcc_injection_single() function entirely if no other callers.  
3. stage.rs:547-558 — The runtime injection block (b1 + vcc_injection_coeff * dc_scale) becomes dead code for WDF stages.
4. stage.rs:441,443 — vcc_injection_coeff and vcc_dc_ramp fields can stay (used by multi-NL stages) but will be 0.0 for all single-NL.

DO NOT touch multi-NL VCC injection (build.rs:1628-1743, stage.rs:2028) — that's a separate system.
DO NOT remove v_max — that's the NR clamp, not signal injection.

IMPORTANT: After removing injection, VCC must NOT be remapped to GND for BJT stages. The collector load path (VCC→Rc→collector) needs VCC as a real supply node in the tree, same as triodes. Check that graph_reduce/SP-reduce handles supply nodes correctly when not remapped.

TEST: Run compile_muff test — stage[0] Q1 should have zero crossings > 0. Sustain pot should affect output (range > 0).

title: Cross-stage loading: boundary-load bindings
description:
Generalize the BA283 output-load fusion (42306285) into first-class boundary-load
bindings: compile-time ANALYSIS of what hangs downstream of every stage boundary,
separated from the POLICY of what the compiler does about it, with the decision
table stored on CompiledPedal for dashboards and triage.

WHY: downstream impedance never reflects back into an upstream stage's scattering
— stages solve against an open circuit. Proven mechanism on the BA283 (ngspice
RL=1G reproduces our unloaded WDF to 3-4 decimals; the loaded golden's -16.1 dB
THD is Q1/Q2 cutoff clipping from load-current demand). The narrow fusion closed
it: LEVEL -0.05 dB, dTHD 0.4 dB, tilt 0.79 dB (servo-off default).

INVESTIGATION MAP (current ba283-stability tip = PR #189):
- Narrow fusion special case: spqr_build.rs:4727 trailing_output_load_group_for_fusion
  (analysis+policy entangled); call sites :662-694 (fuse into build_edges, relabel)
  and :981 (consume standalone trailing stage — same mechanism as blockwise
  coupling consumption at :468-496). Opt-out: PK_OUTPUT_FUSE_DISABLE.
- Ad-hoc boundary metadata today (what the bindings replace/subsume):
  - transformer_gain: Wave on WdfStage/MultiNlStage (pedalkernel-rt stage.rs:1548, :4898) — ratio only, no impedance
  - WiperDivider (processor.rs:1147) — output-pot divider bolted on after a stage idx
  - InterstageLoading (loading.rs:100) — pedal-level I/O only, never stage-to-stage
  - z^-1 delayed-cut carries (boundary_rules.rs) — node + gain scalar
  - stage chain is a bare f64 sample (processor.rs:3869-4360)
- Prior art (consume the lesson, do NOT reopen scope): epic pedalkernel-0h3 —
  binding/drive types were deliberately kept OUT of the neutral network-math types
  (LinearMultiportNetwork); planner/stage layer owns bindings. Controls fan-out
  via StageBinding/ControlTarget (processor.rs:1042).
- Next consumers: pedalkernel-9h2s transformer step-down/load (~19-20 dB, LA-2A
  GAP F family); Klon/RAT/Pultec unloaded output boundaries (WSL/NaN triage).

DESIGN (agreed):
- compiler/boundary_load.rs:
  - BoundaryLoadModel: Unloaded | GroundedResistive{r,edges} | SeriesCapIntoLoad{c,r,edges} | PassiveNetwork{edges}
  - LoadDisposition: FusedUpstream{consumed_group} | Unloaded{reason} (future: ReflectedShunt, ReflectedThroughTransformer)
  - BoundaryLoadBinding { upstream_stage, boundary_node, model, disposition }
  - CompiledPedal carries Vec<BoundaryLoadBinding>
- Sequencing: Child1+Child2 land first (Child1 byte-identical corpus + both
  dashboards unchanged; Child2 visibility table + WSL/NaN triage flags), then
  Child3 (pot loads) and Child4 (transformer-secondary, priority consumer) in parallel.
- Risks: spqr_build.rs is 5929 lines on a shared branch — supervisors fetch +

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: INVESTIGATION (Vera): CONFIRMED hypothesis (1) - transfer-function/gain error in the MNA->biquad derivation, NOT pot-semantics, NOT input calibration. Defect site: MnaSystem::build_iir bilinear-transform of the augmented (caps+VCVS) system at pedalkernel-rt/src/tree.rs:1404 (invoked from pedalkernel/src/compiler/rigid/iir.rs:86). EVIDENCE (compile_via_spqr on mfb_highpass_controlled.pedal, fs=48k): single IIR stage label='C1,C2,Cutoff,R_fb,U1', b=[44.6495,-89.2991,44.6495], a=[1.0,0.020393,-0.979161]. Denominator roots z~=0.979 and z~=-1.0; the pole at z=-1 (Nyquist) is SPURIOUS and bends the response down at HF. ngspice ref (Eop v_op 0 0 v_neg 100000, Rcut 52.5k, Rfb 47k) rises monotonically +20dB/dec across the whole audio band (no HF rolloff). WDF-vs-ngspice deltas: 100Hz +6.0dB, 251Hz +5.8dB, 631Hz +5.0dB, 1001Hz +3.7dB, 2515Hz -0.9dB, 5020Hz -5.8dB, 10020Hz -10.3dB, 20kHz -23.3dB. So WDF is ~+4-6dB HOT through the low/mid passband (matching the bead's low_sine +9.6 / high_sine +8.4) AND wrongly rolls off at HF. RULED OUT: hyp(2) pot-semantics - WDF default 0.5 via [1.0,0.05] maps to 0.525*100k=52.5k, EXACTLY the .spice Rcut=52.5k (verified). hyp(3) input calibration - both decks inject Vin at v_in=C1.a, same convention, comparison is RMS-vs-RMS unnormalized. The error is a wrong continuous->discrete transfer: build_iir mis-places the 2nd pole near Nyquist and scales the passband gain ~+4-6dB too high for this virtual-ground inverting MFB HPF. FIX PROPOSAL: audit build_iir (tree.rs:1404+) augmented bilinear stamping for the VCVS/output-node coupling - the near-ideal VCVS (A=1e5) D-matrix entry + output taken at v_op is mis-conditioning the discretized poles. Validate the analytic H(s)= -sRfb*C2 * (sRcut*C1)/(1+sRcut*C1) form against the emitted biquad; expected: 2 zeros at DC, 1 audio-band pole, upper pole far above fs/2. Beads stay in_progress.

comments.text: INVESTIGATION (Vera): ROOT CAUSE pinned to graph.rs:647-650 (pedalkernel/src/compiler/graph.rs). For the Sallen-Key fixtures (U1.neg->U1.out direct wire), VcvsEdge processing detects neg_node==out_node (unity follower) and executes 'uf.union(id_pos, id_out)'. This is correct for a plain buffer where pos IS the input, but in the SK topology pos is the high-Z reactive-network node (C2.b/R2.a junction) and out drives the SK feedback through R1. Unioning pos into out collapses the SK feedback network and DELETES the active buffer's isolation. Downstream the opamp FlowGroup becomes 'group 0: edges=[U1(Vcvs)]' -> SPQR 'Q-node -> 0 stages' (buffer dropped entirely). EVIDENCE: throwaway trace (compile_via_spqr on sallen_key_highpass/lowpass.pedal): output = -240dB (total silence) at 100/500/1k/5k/10kHz; stages=[WDF,WDF,WDF] passive-only, the active driver absent; trace line 'group 0: feedback=false edges=[U1(Vcvs)]' then 'SPQR result: Q-node -> 0 stages'. ngspice deck (Eop v_op 0 v_pos v_op 100000) gives a proper nonzero SK response. FIX PROPOSAL: a unity follower must NOT union pos->out. Instead keep the opamp as a real VCVS/nullor with V_out = V_pos (out node driven from pos, neg tied to out), so it isolates the reactive network from the load (R_out). The union short-circuits the buffer input to its output. Either (a) skip the union and emit a proper buffer stage that copies V_pos->V_out with neg as the sensed node, or (b) for unity followers contract neg->out only (already the case) and route the FlowGroup so the opamp emits an active buffer stage rather than a 0-stage Q-node self-loop. The defect is the pos<->out union at graph.rs:649. Beads stay in_progress.

title: Bug: CA3080 OTA and LED diode-pair fail to compile — MS-20 filter voices unreachable
description:
Symptom: ms20_lpf.pedal and ms20_hpf.pedal use opamp(ca3080) (OTA) and diode_pair(led). These component types fail to compile or produce incorrect behavior. All tests/ms20_behavior.rs tests are #[ignore]'d with annotation 'MS-20 OTA/LED compile fallback tracked in pedalkernel-jt0.' FilterTopology does not include Ms20 variants; BiValve users cannot select the MS-20 filter.

SPICE validation report (reports/pedalkernel-spice-validation-2026-06-09.md, line 71): 'OTA CA3080 fails compile in rigid fallback: unsupported nonlinear device kind in general MNA.' Active suite: 8 circuits, 2 pass. OTA still compile-fails per improvements report (2026-06-09).

Affected components:
  opamp(ca3080): OTA transfer function is Iout = gm * Vdiff where gm proportional to Iabc (bias current). Differs fundamentally from voltage-mode opamp; requires different WDF model. Bias current Iabc set by DC voltage via NPN transistor bias stage driven by cutoff pot + R_cutoff_floor.
  diode_pair(led): LED pair for soft-clipping resonance feedback. Forward voltage Vf ~1.8V vs silicon 0.7V. If diode_pair exists for silicon, a led variant with adjusted Vf parameter should be straightforward.

Fix requirements:
  1. CA3080 OTA model: implement opamp(ca3080) as voltage-controlled transconductance stage. gm = 19.2 * Iabc (mA/V at room temp). Cutoff control sets DC voltage -> Iabc via NPN bias stage.
  2. LED diode model: diode_pair(led) with Vf ~1.8V parameterized (vs silicon 0.7V).

Pro-side wiring (unblocked once engine compiles both): add ms20_lpf/hpf to bivalve build.rs voices, add blob constants, add Ms20=4 to FilterTopology enum, update TOPOLOGY_NAMES/blob_for/set_topology_idx, update Q parameters in FilterCore::configure(), remove #[ignore] from ms20_behavior.rs. Product bead pedalkernel-jt0 tracks the BiValve product-side wiring.

References: Korg MS-20 service notes; CA3080 datasheet (Intersil/Renesas); Will Pirkle Designing Software Synthesizer Plug-Ins in C++ Ch.14 (OTA filter, LED resonance clipping).

Filed from pedalkernel-pro/crates/bivalve/ENGINE_BUG_MS20_OTA_LED.md (2026-05-28, file not yet shrunk — deferred until feat/acidattack branch merges).

Acceptance criteria: ms20_lpf.pedal and ms20_hpf.pedal compile without error; ms20_behavior.rs tests un-ignored and passing correct frequency responses; FilterTopology::Ms20 variants available to BiValve users.

title: Bug: active 2-pole MFB HPF topology fails to compile — falls back to 1-pole passive RC
description:
Symptom: A Rauch MFB high-pass filter (series C-C input path driving opamp.neg, shunt R to GND/vref, feedback R from neg to out) compiled from a .pedal netlist produces flat or incorrect frequency response — does not exhibit 12dB/oct HPF behavior. Workaround: bivalve-core ships mfb_hpf.pedal as a 1-pole passive RC HPF (C1-series, R_floor shunt) giving 6dB/oct; the second pole is supplied by a runtime biquad layer in FilterCore.

Root cause (hypothesis): WDF compiler opamp analysis pass does not classify the series C-C input path as an MFB HPF topology. Two failure modes observed: (1) treats both caps as a single coupling path and ignores the second pole, or (2) misroutes signal through the vref supply reference when the shunt R connects to vref rather than gnd. MFB LPF (series R-R input, shunt caps) compiles correctly; the HPF dual does not.

Variants tested (all fail HPF behavior):
  C2.b -> U1.neg, R_shunt -> gnd: flat gain, cutoff has zero effect
  C2.b -> U1.neg, R_shunt -> vref: large gain at all freqs, response inverted
  C2.b -> U1.out (mislabeled LPF): acts as LPF with +12dB gain, cutoff works

Repro circuit (.pedal inline):
  pedal "MFB HPF Test" { supply 9V; components { U1: opamp(tl072); C1: cap(10n); C2: cap(10n); Cutoff_R1: pot(100k, b); R_fb: resistor(47k); R_out: resistor(10k) }; nets { in -> C1.a; C1.b -> C2.a; C2.b -> U1.neg; C1.b -> Cutoff_R1.a; Cutoff_R1.b -> gnd; U1.neg -> R_fb.a; R_fb.b -> U1.out; U1.pos -> gnd; U1.out -> R_out.a; R_out.b -> out }; controls { Cutoff_R1.position -> "Cutoff" [1.0, 0.05] = 0.5 } }
  Expected: gain at 100Hz << gain at 10kHz (HPF). Actual: flat gain or wrong response.

Reference: TI SLOA088 "Multiple Feedback Filter Architecture".

Fix requirements: compiler opamp analysis / WDF topology builder must handle: two capacitors in series driving opamp.neg + shunt R to gnd/vref + feedback R from neg to out -> classify as 2-pole MFB HPF, compile to active IIR stage (analogous to how MFB LPF -> Iir or StateSpace stage).

Pro-side context: bivalve-core uses mfb_hpf.pedal as 1-pole passive workaround. Product bead pedalkernel-y5k tracks BiValve product-side wiring; this engine bead tracks the compiler gap. Filed from pedalkernel-pro/crates/bivalve/ENGINE_BUG_MFB_HPF_ACTIVE.md (2026-05-28, file not yet shrunk — deferred until feat/acidattack branch merges).

Acceptance criteria: mfb_hpf.pedal with correct Rauch topology (C-C series input) compiles and produces 12dB/oct HPF frequency response with working cutoff control; no flat-gain fallback.
close_reason: Fixed MFB HPF extraction and added focused repro coverage.

description: While validating the AcidAttack Stinchcombe DSP fallback, the broad acidattack-core diode_ladder test filter also selected engine_blockwise_gap tests. Those BKM tests panic in pedalkernel/src/compiler/blockwise.rs:2483 with index out of bounds: len is 3 but index is 3, during coupling MNA with 3 block ports. This is separate from the DSP fallback path, whose focused diode_ladder module tests pass.

title: Add resonant simple WDF AcidAttack filter
description: Follow-up to the bootable SimpleWdf two-pole LPF: add a stable resonant two-pole/Sallen-Key-style alternate .pedal for AcidAttack hardware testing. Keep it separate from the full tb303_filter.pedal and preserve DSP fallback. Validate cutoff response, resonance effect, non-silence, and Daisy build before making it the hardware default.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: Important contract for resonant/simple WDF: do not drive cutoff by recomputing pot controls at CV rate. Current SimpleWdf two-pole only uses the Cutoff pot as a compiled control and terminates cv_cutoff through a bleed resistor, so CV is effectively inert. Correct fix is to bind cv_cutoff port voltage to a runtime modulation sink such as JFET Vgs/OTA gain/diff-pair tail current, with the pot as control-rate bias/offset.

title: Define stable C ABI for Patch.Init hardware services
description: Define extern C functions/types between Rust DSP and C++ libDaisy: init, start audio, read controls/CV, read buttons, write CV outs/LED, panic/status hooks. Keep ABI POD-only, no exceptions/RTTI/alloc crossing boundary.

title: Integrate Rust AcidAttack DSP behind libDaisy audio callback
description: Wire Rust AcidAttack/PedalKernel DSP into the C++ libDaisy audio callback through the C ABI. C++ owns audio ISR and buffers; Rust processes mono IN_L to OUT_L and optional VCO/debug output. Avoid heap and keep f32 ABI.
close_reason: AcidAttack Patch.Init FFI now instantiates shared acidattack-core engine behind libDaisy audio callback; generated bootloader .bin links successfully.

title: Use C++ libDaisy FFI for Patch.Init/Patch.SM hardware layer
description: Epic: Use current Electro-Smith C++ libDaisy behind a narrow C ABI for Patch.Init/Patch.SM firmware. Rust keeps AcidAttack/PedalKernel DSP and control logic; C++ owns board init, bootloader-compatible build/link, audio/ADC/DAC/GPIO hardware.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: Implemented first FFI slice in pedalkernel-pro: durable Arm toolchain path, upstream C++ libDaisy BOOT_SRAM Patch.Init blink baseline, Rust AcidAttack DSP split into no_std staticlib/rlib, and C++ blink target now links/calls the Rust C ABI. Next step is replacing blink loop with libDaisy audio/control callback integration.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: Moved the Patch.Init/Patch.SM libDaisy C++ runtime shell into pedalkernel-daisy. AcidAttack now supplies only a small app descriptor with Rust DSP C ABI callbacks. Shared shell maps CV_1-4 panel controls, CV_5-8 external CV, B7 shift, B8 waveform, IN_L to Rust DSP, OUT_L VCF, OUT_R VCO, CV_OUT_1 env, CV_OUT_2/C1 heartbeat LED. Added pedalkernel-daisy host tests for Patch.Init normalization.

title: Port current libDaisy Patch.Init/Patch.SM subset to Rust
description: Epic: Replace stale libdaisy-rust assumptions with a focused Rust port of the current Electro-Smith libDaisy subset needed for Patch.Init/Patch.SM AcidAttack firmware. Scope excludes unrelated boards/devices until Patch.Init boots, blinks, reads controls, and runs mono audio reliably.

title: Make pedalkernel-rt compile cleanly with Wave=f32
description: AcidAttack Daisy firmware exposed that pedalkernel-rt does not compile cleanly for thumbv7em-none-eabihf with Wave=f32. Metering, thermal/device solvers, oscillator/envelope/glide, processor paths still mix f64 state with math::Wave helpers. AcidAttack Daisy is temporarily using a local f32 DSP engine instead of acidattack-core/pedalkernel-rt until the shared runtime is made M7-safe.
close_reason: pedalkernel-rt source now uses Wave throughout runtime paths; desktop uses f64 alias and thumbv7em-none-eabihf no_std uses f32 alias. Verified cargo test -p pedalkernel-rt, cargo check -p pedalkernel, and cargo +nightly check -p pedalkernel-rt --target thumbv7em-none-eabihf --no-default-features -Zbuild-std=core,alloc.

title: Investigate AcidAttack BKM response and subharmonic regression
description: Hard CSV/FFT read shows current AcidAttack BKM k=0 response may be worse than the earlier 2.69dB fit and FFT may contain a dominant 55Hz subharmonic on a 110Hz probe. Add focused validation that distinguishes measurement artifact from real period-doubling/DC drift: time-domain period-2 check, input-frequency tracking of subharmonic, input-level sweep threshold, and compare against the previous saved response data. Do not tune the oracle; use this to isolate whether the runtime, .pedal, or exporter setup regressed.

title: Match TB303 BKM k=0 to full Stinchcombe 10-pole including 97.5rad pole
description: The test oracle was corrected to include Stinchcombe's missing (s+97.5) coupling pole. tb303_compare_bkm_forced_serial_and_htb_shape is now red: BKM k=0 best fit is fc=4929.4Hz with max_abs_err=4.36dB. The .pedal/coupling-cap shelf likely needs the additional low-frequency coupling pole modeled rather than relaxing the threshold.

title: Add TB303 coupling-cap shelf validation
description: Add/repair TB303 low-resonance validation for the 10-pole coupling-cap shelf before resonance tuning. The goal is to model real input/output/feedback coupling caps in the .pedal and ensure BKM lowpass response matches the published 10-pole spectrum shape without runtime shortcuts.

title: Bound TB303 BKM resonance against 10-pole reference
description: Current coupled BKM resonance path is alive but unstable/over-gained: tb303_bkm_resonance_control_changes_cutoff_band reports roughly +17.5 dB at 500 Hz, +124.9 dB at 2 kHz, and +141.5 dB at 5 kHz for Resonance=0.85. Add regression assertions against a sane 10-pole/Stinchcombe-derived envelope and fix feedback gain/sign/normalization in the coupling network, not via a synthetic feedback port.

title: Fix AcidAttack BKM cutoff control response
description: AcidAttack DSP ladder responds correctly, but the compiled BKM filter path is cutoff-dead in filter_engine_controls_have_measurable_effect: BKM cutoff effect at 5kHz is about 0.00 dB while DSP is >100 dB. BKM resonance now moves, so focus on cutoff CV/control propagation into the coupled blockwise K-method runtime and port/state update path.

title: Fix AcidAttack serial WDF control response
description: AcidAttack Serial WDF filter path is still control-dead in filter_engine_controls_have_measurable_effect: cutoff effect at 5kHz is +0.00 dB and resonance max boost is +0.00 dB. Rack is forced to DSP until this compiled path has meaningful cutoff/resonance response.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: Added bootable experimental SimpleWdf mode for AcidAttack: separate tb303_filter_simple_wdf.pedal, compiled as its own postcard blob, selectable as FilterEngineMode::SimpleWdf, and set as Daisy default for hardware WDF testing. It is a non-resonant two-pole RC WDF baseline; resonant follow-up filed as pedalkernel-34u.

title: Add realtime delayed BKM solve mode
description: Add an explicit one-sample delayed coupled Blockwise K-method solve mode for realtime AcidAttack/VCV use. Keep CoupledNewton as the delay-free validation/reference path, and route AcidAttack BKM builds to the delayed mode to avoid per-sample 16-port Newton/Jacobian CPU spikes.

title: Fix AcidAttack serial WDF filter silence
description: After replacing BKM block Jacobian finite differences with K-table/tree derivatives, AcidAttack BKM vco_in reaches output (RMS 0.0666, max_jump 0.071), but compiled_filter_vco_port_reaches_output_in_bkm_and_serial still shows Serial WDF RMS=0. The serial forced-blockwise path is silent and should be debugged separately from BKM.

title: Tighten TB303 active resonance against 10-pole reference
description: Production tb303_filter.pedal now routes resonance through an active inverting feedback stage and BKM sees a controlled resonance boost, but the k=0 BKM-vs-10-pole fit regressed versus the previous passive baseline. Follow up by modeling the exact 303 feedback HP/coupling network and adding a no-runaway/high-resonance bound test against the 10-pole reference.

title: Model TB303 resonance feedback polarity stage
description: Side-aware BKM now routes the passive resonance path through existing rung ports and restores non-silent lowpass output, but increasing Resonance attenuates cutoff-band gain instead of creating a peak. This likely means the .pedal is missing the real 303 feedback polarity/inverting stage (or BKM side-aware port polarity still maps the feedback node with opposite sign). Add a first-principles resonance feedback model and validate against H_tb/10-pole resonance curves.

title: BKM resonance matrix delta is passive coupling contribution
description: Add a coupling-matrix contract test proving Resonance=k changes only the passive feedback-network contribution relative to Resonance=0, with no added synthetic source port and no unrelated topology disturbance.

title: BKM resonance sweep creates monotonic peak
description: Add a TB303 BKM regression sweeping Resonance from 0 to high values and measuring peak gain near cutoff. The peak should increase monotonically enough to prove the passive resonance network is live without using a synthetic source port.

title: BKM resonance=0 matches no-feedback topology
description: Add a TB303 regression comparing full tb303_filter.pedal at Resonance=0 against an equivalent no-resonance topology. The BKM frequency sweep should match numerically so adding a resonance path cannot disturb the zero-resonance linear backbone.

title: Hoist BKM coupled Newton workspace and analytic K-table derivatives
description: The dense all-port finite-difference Jacobian has been replaced with a sparse block-aware derivative, but coupled Newton still allocates per sample and still finite-differences each block boundary. Next step: preallocate Newton buffers on BlockwiseKMethodStage and expose KTable/block derivative lookup so db/da is analytic and table-backed for Cortex-M7/VCV CPU headroom.
close_reason: Implemented KTable derivative lookups and WDF tree gain propagation for BKM coupled Newton Jacobian; removed per-block finite-difference derivative path and verified against existing finite-difference Jacobian test.

title: Map TB303 10-pole resonance k to AcidAttack controls
description: The added 10-pole reference is useful at k=0, but nonzero published k is not yet mapped to our resonance control scale and currently gives misleading diagnostic magnitudes. Add a documented mapping/calibration before using nonzero-k 10-pole comparisons as pass/fail validation.

title: Correct TB303 filter output and resonance feedback nodes
description: Current tb303_filter.pedal takes output from Q4.emitter and feeds resonance back to Q1.base in the cascade model. After the coupled ladder topology is corrected, audit and wire output/resonance feedback to the real 303-equivalent ladder nodes and feedback coupling path so resonance excites the coupled ladder instead of a serial cascade.

title: Separate TB303 audio input from cutoff CV injection
description: tb303_filter.pedal currently sums audio_in, vco_in, and cv_cutoff into Q1.base through resistors. Real 303 audio enters through the bottom differential pair while cutoff CV drives the expo converter/current source. Separate these domains to prevent CV bleed and make cutoff response follow the intended current/exponential control path.

title: Fix TB303 BKM cutoff pot bias path
description: BKM direct cascade is lowpass when cv_cutoff is explicitly driven, and feedback-port injection no longer bypasses the ladder at Resonance=0. Remaining bug: with cv_cutoff at 0V, the Cutoff pot/bias path alone does not restore a lowpass cascade; ignored regression tb303_bkm_cutoff_pot_without_cv_is_lowpass documents 100Hz and 10kHz nearly equal. Need derive and feed the pot-derived diode operating bias into the blockwise K-method contract without hardcoding TB303-specific control names.

title: Fix BKM composite block port reflection
description: TB303 BKM tests show isolated first diode rung matches forced-serial WDF after biased K-table/control-polarity fixes, but BKM cascade loses pole order: block outputs are flat and coupling loop feeds nonlinear-root a_root into the coupling port. Investigate and replace with the correct composite block-port wave variable so the coupling matrix sees the block port, not the internal nonlinear root.

title: Fix TB303 BKM shallow 4-pole slope
description: Filter readiness run shows tb303_bkm_direct_path_is_lowpass fails: BKM core direct path is lowpass but only 100Hz=0.288376 vs 10kHz=0.123813, ratio +7.3dB. A 4-pole 303 ladder should have a much stronger high-frequency rolloff. Focus bug hunt on BKM cascade/block state extraction, per-rung source impedance, and coupling injection before changing .pedal parameters.

title: Fix TB303 BKM weak resonance peak
description: Filter readiness run shows tb303_resonance_creates_peak fails: 2kHz gain is flat=3.9597, resonant=4.7187, ratio=1.19x, below the existing >1.3x readiness threshold. Resonance coupling exists but is under-scaled or injected at the wrong wave/voltage point. Investigate BKM coupling scattering, feedback port map, Resonance pot inversion/resistance update, and output feedback voltage sign/scale.
close_reason: BKM resonance feedback port now participates in coupled solve; AcidAttack TB303 .pedal tail/feedback path now produces measurable resonance gain.

title: Fix BiValve filter control movement in product regression matrix
description: The new product regression matrix references pedalkernel-pro/crates/bivalve .pedal sources directly. Ignored audio capture reports Cutoff has 0.00dB/diff movement on MS-20 LPF/HPF, Sallen-Key LPF/HPF, and MFB LPF; Resonance has 0.0000 diff on MS-20 LPF/HPF and MFB LPF; MFB LPF default output is silent. TDD these from the product matrix before making the audio matrix a default gate.

title: Fix AcidBath product regression failures
description: The new product regression matrix references pedalkernel-pro/crates/acidattack .pedal sources directly. Ignored audio capture currently reports tb303_filter.pedal panics in diode WDF render with assertion failed: w > 0.0, and tb303_vca.pedal VCA_Gain has 0.00dB measured output movement despite healthy default output. TDD these from the product matrix before making the audio matrix a default gate.

title: Fix Screamer/SD1 tone controls with measurable output effect
description: Legends validation should not pass by binding-only checks. Stricter VST-path validation shows Screamer and SD-1 Tone are bound but produce 0.000% measurable output change, while Goldenrod Treble and Ratking Filter move spectrum. Root cause appears in the kernel tone-blend path for 3-terminal tone pots / unity-buffer passive stage output, not VST settings alone.

title: Add Legends VST characterization regression suite
description: Design and implement release-regression tests for the four launch Legends pedals: Goldenrod, Ratking, Screamer, and SD-1. Replace brittle single-point audio hashes and stale diagnostic coverage with metric-based harmonic fingerprints, stepped frequency sweeps, pot sweeps, input-level distortion curves, output normalization checks, compiler topology/control-binding parity, and VST embedded-blob parity. Baselines should be JSON with tolerances and a regen path, with fast CI and full release tiers.

title: Fix AcidAttack WDF cutoff CV AC response
description: Full frequency sweep of tb303_filter.pedal through process_ports shows identical settled AC response for cv_cutoff=-1V, 0V, +1V, and +3V. Existing peak test sees only a small level shift, but cutoff CV is not moving the filter corner in the compiled BKM/WDF path. Need TDD regression using settled AC RMS at multiple frequencies, then root-cause whether cv_cutoff is treated only as additive signal/bias instead of controlling ladder operating current/k-table state.
close_reason: Fixed: added normal-diode and TB303 ExplicitSingleDiode cutoff AC regressions, runtime cutoff source-R modulation, reversible sweep coverage, and BJT-to-diode constructor reuse.

title: Fix AcidAttack BKM runtime filter response
description: Current BKM compiler path now verifies tb303_filter.pedal node wiring, keeps two-port diode ladder rung caps inside BKM blocks, compiles a two-rung diode feedback ladder to BKM, and recomputes the resonance coupling matrix. Remaining red tests show runtime/output semantics are still wrong: tb303_bkm_direct_path_is_lowpass is slightly high-frequency rising, and tb303_resonance_creates_peak shows no 2kHz peak. Investigate KMethodBlock cascade voltage extraction/state update and feedback injection semantics rather than SPQR grouping.

title: Make AcidAttack ladder mode explicit and tested
description: AcidAttack embeds a WDF TB-303 filter blob but defaults use_dsp_ladder=true with no public feature/runtime selection and comments saying WDF is disabled until it produces correct lowpass. Tests named WDF/spice_validation actually exercise the DSP ladder through AcidAttack::process(), so they do not validate the WDF path. Add an explicit DSP-vs-WDF feature/API contract and tests that prove each mode's response and performance.

title: Complete AcidAttack VCV control/sample-rate wiring
description: VCV shim passes lifecycle tests but leaves important behavior unwired: RESONANCE_CV input is declared/configured but never applied; Drive shift-layer control is TODO with no engine API; engine sample_rate is never updated from VCV ProcessArgs so envelopes/glide/filter timing assume 48k at all Rack sample rates; Audio R is a raw VCO debug tap while the panel/output label implies audio R. Add behavior tests through the FFI/module boundary.
close_reason: Completed VCV wiring gaps in scope: resonance CV is applied, sample rate is forwarded to the engine, OUT_R mirrors audio instead of debug VCO, CXX FFI/header updated, and Rack plugin build passes.

title: Fix AcidAttack core VCA and glide regressions
description: cargo test --manifest-path crates/acidattack/acidattack-core/Cargo.toml currently fails 5 tests: pitch_glide_during_slide arrives instantly; vca_closed_is_silent outputs ~0.95; accent_boosts_level is clipped equal to normal; dc_blocker_removes_offset leaves ~0.296 DC; fast_tanh_accuracy exceeds tolerance. These directly undermine 303 behavior: slide, VCA closure, accent dynamics, coupling cap behavior, and saturation accuracy.
close_reason: Completed non-WDF AcidAttack behavior fixes: explicit slide gate, VCA/accent/DC/tanh calibration, and behavior tests.

title: Wire AcidAttack Daisy runtime
description: AcidAttack Daisy is still a blink/link scaffold: no RTIC audio callback, no SAI/DMA audio path, no Patch.Init control mapping, no flashable audio firmware behavior. It also fails standalone Cargo build because acidattack-daisy is under the pedalkernel-pro workspace tree but not a member/excluded workspace root. Bring it to parity with the Legends Daisy runtime: bounded allocator, audio IN_L/OUT_L, Patch.Init controls/gates/CV, firmware build, objcopy .bin, and host adapter tests.

title: Expose Patch.Init ADC_9-ADC_12 panel knobs
description: Patch.Init has four separate 0-5V panel pots on ADC_9 through ADC_12, while the single-pedal Daisy firmware currently uses default base knob positions plus CV1-CV4 offsets over those controls. libdaisy-rust's GPIO wrapper in this repo does not expose all Patch.Init pot pins, notably PC2/PC3 for ADC_12/ADC_11, so add a local Patch.Init board wrapper or extend the GPIO abstraction before reading panel knobs directly.
close_reason: User clarified Patch.Init wiring: CV_1-CV_4 are knob inputs and CV_5-CV_8 are CV offsets, so no separate ADC_9-ADC_12 panel knob support is needed for this firmware.

title: Wire single-pedal Daisy audio, CV ADC, and model button HAL
description: The single-pedal Daisy crate now has a host-tested mono Legends adapter with four CV-over-knob controls and button edge cycling, plus a firmware target scaffold that links for Patch.SM. Remaining work is the hardware layer: sample Patch.SM audio input, four CV ADCs over K1/K2/K3/input gain, and a physical button into LegendsDaisy::set_select_button inside the libdaisy audio callback.
close_reason: Wired single-pedal Daisy firmware: RTIC app initializes libdaisy System, processes mono audio in DMA callback, samples CV1-CV4 over controls on TIM2, and uses Patch.SM Gate In 1 as model-select button.

title: Add single-pedal Daisy firmware wrapper
description: single-pedal-core is target-neutral and tested, but there is no single-pedal-daisy firmware crate. Existing Daisy firmware crates for AcidAttack, BiValve, and DrummerBoy are blink/link scaffolds only. Add a Daisy wrapper crate that depends on single-pedal-core, initializes hardware/audio, maps controls, and builds for thumbv7em-none-eabihf.

title: Provide init-time allocator for single-pedal Daisy
description: single-pedal-core deserializes postcard CompiledPedal blobs into alloc-backed runtime structures in Legends::new() and on pedal switch. Current Daisy blink scaffolds use a NoHeap allocator that panics on allocation, which is incompatible with loading embedded pedal blobs. Add a bounded init-time allocator strategy and ensure no allocation happens in the audio callback.

title: Wire Daisy audio and controls for single-pedal Legends
description: pedalkernel-daisy exposes a host-tested BlockProcessor contract, but current firmware scaffolds do not initialize SAI/DMA audio or call a processor from an audio callback. Implement a single-pedal BlockProcessor adapter for Legends, map knobs/CV/switches to pedal select, three controls, and input gain, set sample rate at prepare/init, and add host tests for channel handling and no-allocation process_block behavior.

title: Investigate Screamer and SD-1 tone audio path
description: The new 12-pot runtime regression shows Screamer and SD-1 Tone controls bind, smooth, and mutate their WDF leaf resistance. Existing pot_sweep_tests::screamer_tone_changes_spectrum and sd1_tone_changes_spectrum still report identical 200 Hz / 5 kHz output at low/high Tone settings. Investigate whether the tone-stage output probe/audio path ignores the moved leaf, or whether the old spectral measurement is stale for these low-impact tone circuits.

title: Replace Goldenrod THD-only regression with path-specific behavior tests
description: Add Goldenrod/Klon tests that measure the intended behavior directly: gain-stage level before clipping, clipped-path harmonic growth, clean feedforward reduction as gain increases, tone shelf movement, and final output blend. The current THD-only assertion is too blunt for a clean/dirty crossfade circuit.
close_reason: Replaced Goldenrod THD-only expectations with path-specific crossfade, pot movement, output movement, and bounded terminal tests.

title: Make IIR pot bindings role-aware
description: Replace generic IirPotBinding behavior with explicit pot roles such as feedback resistance, input/ground-leg resistance, feedforward/crossfade path, and tone shelf. Goldenrod/Klon-style controls need role-aware coefficient and blend updates instead of treating every IIR pot as feedback Rf or a generic table dimension.

title: Enforce compiler/runtime feature parity for embedded pedals
description: Prevent VST/embed builds from compiling pedal blobs with a feature set that differs from the runtime deserializer/processor. In particular, if pedalkernel-rt enables biquad-table, the build-time pedalkernel compiler dependency must also enable biquad-table. Add a build-time assertion or regression that confirms expected table data is present in embedded blobs.

title: Add control capability contract tests per stage type
description: Add focused tests for every stage type that can contain/bind pots: WDF, IIR, MultiNL, BlackFeedback, and BlockwiseKMethod. Each test should bind a control, sweep it, and assert the stage's runtime state changes appropriately: leaf resistance, gain, coefficient table lookup, scattering recompute, or BKM block tree resistance.

title: Make control binding stage-owned
description: Move control lookup and mutation responsibility out of spqr_control.rs and into stage-owned APIs, e.g. Stage::bind_control()/Stage::set_control_pot(). This should reduce duplicated stage introspection and prevent new stage types from binding controls without runtime mutation support.
close_reason: Completed stage-owned pot discovery and mutation slice

title: Implement WDF-coupled 808 BJT shunt bridged-T
description: Replace the removed IIR sweep metadata hack with an honest WDF/MultiNL-coupled implementation for the 808 kick v2 transistor shunt. The BJT across the bridged-T resistor must be solved in-circuit with the resonator state, not by mutating IIR coefficients or applying hardcoded decay multipliers. Add tests proving v2 keeps sharper transient than v1 while preserving usable body/decay.

title: Tune 808 kick v2 decay length
description: 808 Kick v2 now has bounded output and pitch sweep, but subjective test indicates the tail decays too quickly. Quantify v1/v2 decay times, add a regression for minimum usable tail length, then adjust sweep/loading/voice values without reintroducing clipping.

title: Model 808 kick v2 BJT sweep inside resonator
description: 808 Kick v2 output is bounded and serial order is fixed, but Q_sweep is currently bypassed from the serial chain and does not yet modulate the U1 bridged-T resonator impedance. Add regressions that prove v2 has pitch/sweep behavior distinct from v1, then implement a circuit-honest coupling path.
close_reason: Added BJT shunt pitch sweep model with headroom and pitch-sweep regressions

title: Fix 808 kick v2 output level and stage ordering
description: 808 Kick v2 now compiles after BJT shunt classification, but output peaks around +1 dBFS and compiled stage order appears wrong: BJT MultiNL and U2 BlackFeedback precede U1 bridged-T IIR. TDD regressions for output health and circuit sequencing, then fix compiler ordering/loading.
close_reason: Fixed with TDD regressions for 808 Kick v2 output headroom and serial stage order

title: Classify BJT switch/modulator separately from amplifier flow
description: 808 Kick v2 puts Q_sweep collector-emitter in parallel with R1 of the bridged-T resonator. signal_flow currently treats every BJT as an amplifier active element, includes collector/emitter as output nodes, and Tarjan SCC groups U1+Q_sweep into one generic MultiNL stage. That bypasses existing bridged-T resonator detection and produces weak output. Add flow classification for BJT-as-switch/variable-resistor so it does not create directed active flow, while preserving BJT amplifier grouping for common-emitter/common-collector stages. Add regression based on 808_kick_v2.
close_reason: Fixed with BJT shunt flow classification, BJT MultiNL routing, and regressions

title: Enable collapse_nl compile path for whole-circuit MultiNL filters
description: Diode ladder HP output is an early named out tap while the ladder is a nonlinear load. Normal SPQR grouping serializes through the ladder and loses the named tap. Implement CompileOptions::collapse_nl to compile all circuit edges into one MultiNL stage, then use it for diode ladder blobs.
close_reason: Implemented collapse_nl and validated diode ladder LP/HP blobs

title: Support named out extraction for MultiNL stages
description: General MultiNL compiler sets extract_coeffs=None and falls back to output_port, so named out behind a passive pad/tap is not extracted. Add regression and compiler/runtime fix.
close_reason: Added regression and fixed MultiNL named output extraction

title: 2-terminal pot scattering (variable resistor mode)
description: Engine issue #1. Pots used as 2-terminal variable resistors (e.g. RATKING filter pot) don't modulate the circuit — engine only supports 3-terminal voltage divider pots. Need to detect 2-terminal pot usage and convert to equivalent WDF variable resistor with proper scattering recompute. Blocks: RATKING filter, potentially other pedals with rheostat-mode pots.

title: Small-value pot MNA sensitivity
description: Engine issue #2. Small pots (e.g. 1kΩ FIZZ fuzz pot) have negligible impedance swing vs surrounding components. Combined with throttled MNA recompute (every 32 samples), the pot delta is lost. Options: reduce throttle interval for small pots, analytical sensitivity check, or interpolated scattering tables. See MNA.md for strategies. Blocks: FIZZ fuzz pot.

title: Boundary-load recording for blockwise-path stages (5/13 fleet read empty-table)
description: C2 finding: the blockwise compile fork records NO boundary-load rows — 5/13 examples/pedals (dyna_comp, boss_dm2, memory_man, fuzz_face, sd1) read 'no-analysis (empty table)', indistinguishable from never-analyzed. Either hoist the recording above the blockwise fork in spqr_build.rs or have the blockwise path record its own rows (analysis is policy-free and reusable). Needed for full-fleet triage coverage; not needed for C3/C4.

title: compile_cache_key lacks schema fingerprint — CompiledPedal field changes poison warm postcard caches
description: Found during pedalkernel-lkf1.1 gating: compile_cache_key has NO schema version/fingerprint, so ANY CompiledPedal field addition/removal makes warm target/test-cache postcard blobs deserialize-fail (DeserializeUnexpectedEnd) — manifested as 20 deterministic tb303 false-flips during byte-identical gating until the cache was cleared. Cold CI caches unaffected; every future schema change trips this for local/warm runs and corrupts corpus SET comparisons (a gating hazard for exactly the kind of byte-identical refactors we rely on). Cheap fix: fold a schema version or type-layout fingerprint (e.g. const bumped alongside CompiledPedal changes, or hash of a schema descriptor) into the cache key so stale blobs miss instead of failing. Acceptance: adding a dummy serde(default) field to CompiledPedal no longer yields deserialize errors on a warm cache; stale entries are treated as misses.

title: Thermal-voltage sweep: retire remaining 25C Vt constants (JFET/diode/OTA) for ngspice 27C CODATA
description:
Retire the remaining 25 C thermal-voltage constants for the ngspice-matching
value. Precedent: the BJT fix (SPICE_VT_27C in pedalkernel/src/model_lookup.rs)
— vt 0.02585 (25 C) vs ngspice TEMP=TNOM=27 C with CODATA-2018 constants
(Vt = 1.380649e-23*300.15/1.602176634e-19 ~ 25.8649 mV) was a systematic
+0.9% Ib / +1.3% Ic error that a feedback network amplified into a 40 mV DC
root offset (BA283). The same constant class remains in every other junction
device and will bite every diode/JFET feedback circuit validated against
ngspice at default temperature.

SITES (production, ba283-stability tip):
- pedalkernel-rt/src/elements/nonlinear/jfet.rs:14 — const VT = 0.02585 (gate junction)
- pedalkernel-rt/src/elements/nonlinear/diode.rs:373-539 — ~13 model presets
  n_vt: N * 25.85e-3 (silicon/germanium/LED/schottky/zener) + n_vt_fwd/n_vt_rev;
  NOTE the "Verified:" clamp derivations at :448/:476 compute limits FROM
  0.02585 — keep internally consistent.
- pedalkernel-rt/src/stage.rs:3018 — ideality_ratio = base.n_vt / 0.02585
  (Vt_ref normalization) — MUST move in lockstep with the diode presets or
  extracted ideality silently shifts.

title: Grouped-NR globalization: line-search/Armijo backtracking + junction limiting (fix multi-BJT divergence)
description: CURRENT damping (pedalkernel-rt elements/nonlinear/solver.rs:1033-1052) is crude: per-component, dv halved ONCE only if |dv|>5.0V, then hard-clamp to v_clamp_port. PROBLEMS: (1) NOT a line search — never checks the step reduces residual ‖F‖; (2) per-COMPONENT cap breaks the Newton DIRECTION (scales some components not others); (3) 5V threshold is absurd for a junction (Vt=26mV) — sub-5V overshoots pass full; (4) the hard clamp PINS divergent iterates at the rails -> ping-pong. On stiff coupled exponential-junction multi-BJT (n_nl>=4) it diverges/pins: 24-iter cap, residual ~4, from a CORRECT seed -> Vbe/Vce railed -> multi-BJT gain collapses to unity (the BA283/xref bug). Single-BJT survives (mild). FIX = globalized damped Newton: (1) LINE SEARCH — scale the WHOLE delta vector by lambda, Armijo backtrack (lambda*=0.5) until ‖F(v-lambda*delta)‖ < ‖F(v)‖ (monotone residual); (2) SPICE-style JUNCTION VOLTAGE LIMITING (pnjlim) — cap per-iter Vbe change to a few Vt to avoid exp() blowup; (3) clamp only as last-resort safety. SUCCESS: 2-BJT reproducer NR CONVERGES (residual->tol, monotone, no rail-pin) where it now diverges; single-BJT still converges; report restored gain (+83 no-fb / +18.7 fb) — note gain restoration ALSO needs known_a (separate). TESTS REQUIRED: unit test that grouped-NR converges on the stiff coupled-junction reproducer (encodes the bug, fails on old damping), monotone-residual assertion, single-BJT regression, full goldens. ALSO dump known_a residual at the ngspice op-point as a diagnostic for the known_a workstream.

title: Adapt the WDF input port to its real Thévenin impedance (kill hardcoded r_adapted=1000Ω) — the BA283 level/scaling deficit
description: SEPARATE bug from the op-point/servo (oz1z): general.rs:760-761 r_nl_default=1000.0 + r_adapted=1000.0 are HARDCODED placeholders for the input voltage-source port (used :821 build_wdf_ports, :1251/:1413 second assemble site). The input port should adapt to the REAL driving impedance it sees (ba283 ~2k2), not 1000Ω; the mismatch divides the injected input wave wrong = pure ~300× LEVEL deficit, shape-correct (0dB normalized RMS). FIX (WDF-correct, from engine-adapted-input-port-impedance memory): adapt the input port resistance to the Thévenin impedance from the PASSIVE MNA — iterate to drive the port self-reflection to ~0 (standard WDF adaptation), NO magic number. NOT device-aware (folding device Jacobians DOUBLE-COUNTS the grouped-NR coupling — user's confirmed insight; prior device-aware attempt got only 3x -49.5->-40.5 AND regressed, reverted 07ac76a). Cover BOTH injection paths: MultiNL s_nl_adapted (ba283) + single-BJT WDF-root+K-table. TEST: ba283 with PK_SERVO_ENABLE (op-point held) — does it close ~0dB? + measure level recovery from the port fix alone. RISK: r_adapted feeds ALL circuits — FULL golden no-regression is the hard gate; if WDF-correct adaptation regresses circuits accidentally-OK at 1000Ω, understand + gate, don't ship regressions. comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
MEASUREMENT (combined-measure branch = adapted-input-port + merged main #181/#182/#183). No engine logic changed: one gated eprintln (PK_RADAPT_TRACE) in general.rs derive_scattering + a new measurement test pedalkernel-validate/tests/ba283_combined_measure.rs. Build green (pedalkernel + validate, --features diag). Disk OK (no ENOSPC). BA283 / neve1073_ba283 golden, 1kHz/0.1V, Gain=0.5, SR48k.

Both fixes confirmed present:
  - Input-port Thévenin adaptation: general.rs:897-992 (iterative, drives input-VS-port self-reflection→0)
  - DC servo: general.rs:1855-1928, gated PK_SERVO_ENABLE (NOTE: lives in general.rs, NOT stage.rs as the task stated)

RESULTS TABLE
                       | A: input-port fix only (servo OFF) | B: BOTH (servo ON)
 (1) raw level vs gold | -32.19 dB                          | -33.34 dB
 (2) r_adapted / ratio | 162.09 Ω  = 0.162x of old 1000 Ω   | 162.09 Ω = 0.162x (identical — servo doesn't touch port R)
 (3) norm-RMS (shape)  | -6.90 dB                           | -5.85 dB
 (4) THD WDF/golden    | -105.2 / -28.5 dB (|Δ|76.8)        | -51.5 / -28.5 dB (|Δ|23.0)
 (5) Q2/2N3055 op-pt   | Vbe 0.486 V, Ic 8.50e-4 A, gm .033 | Vbe 0.478 V, Ic 5.91e-4 A, gm .023

VERDICT
- Does it close? NO. Residual is ~32-33 dB LEVEL deficit with both fixes on. Servo did not improve level (slightly worse, -32.2→-33.3).
- Input-port fix recovered ~17 dB on its own (documented -49.5 baseline → -32.2). That is the dominant win, NOT the servo.
- Can port impedance explain the gain? NO. Adapted r_adapted=162 Ω is LOWER than the old 1000 Ω placeholder (ratio 0.162x), the OPPOSITE direction and ~6x, nowhere near the 100-300x the level gap needs. The Thévenin port impedance alone cannot account for the deficit. (It already gave its ~17 dB; the placeholder was too HIGH, not too low.)
- Is it pure-gain / shape 1:1? NO — not after the servo turns on the device's nonlinearity. Shape (norm-RMS) is ~ -6 dB either way (decent but not 1:1, ~50% relative error). THD tells the real story: servo OFF the WDF is nearly linear (THD -105 dB) vs golden's Class-A -28 dB; servo ON the op-point holds enough to produce THD -51 dB — moving TOWARD golden but still 23 dB short of golden's harmonic content. So the residual is a COMBINED op-point/loop-gain deficit (device under-driven → too little gain AND too little distortion), not a clean scalar gain you can normalize away.

CAVEAT (#5): only Q2/2N3055 surfaces at runtime — BA283 compiles via the Blockwise path (3 NL blocks → monolithic), and TR1(Q3)/TR2(Q1) live in the BlockwiseStage which exposes no runtime op-point accessor; only the MultiNl-routed 2N3055 is readable. The harness's ba283_runtime_nr also can't print (its max_resid<1e-2 assert trips first: 28 servo-OFF, 6.8 servo-ON, both pre-existing). Reported Q2 honestly; TR1/TR2 runtime Vbe not available without an engine change (out of scope for a measurement). harmonic-mag-err=0.00 is an artifact (scaled WDF harmonics sit below the -100 dB floor → no bins scored); the THD pair is the valid spectral read.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: COMBINED MEASUREMENT (branch combined-measure = input-port fix + merged main #183 servo). VERDICT: does NOT close (~-32/-33 dB both on). KEY NUMBERS: (A) input-port fix only servo-OFF = -32.19 dB = +17 dB vs -49.5 baseline — the input-port fix is a REAL ~17dB win. r_adapted = 162Ω (0.162× of old 1000Ω) — the placeholder was too HIGH; correct value is LOWER; ratio CANNOT explain 100-300× and is the wrong direction. (B) both servo-ON = -33.34 dB (servo marginally WORSE on level once port is fixed). NOT pure gain: servo-OFF WDF is nearly LINEAR (THD -105dB) vs golden Class-A -28.5dB; servo-ON adds real distortion (THD -51dB, toward golden but 23dB short). Normalized-RMS shape error ~-6dB (not 1:1). So residual = combined gain+distortion under-drive (loop-gain/Class-A reproduction), NOT a scalar level. Q2/2N3055 servo-ON Ic 5.9e-4 (SPICE 218µ, still ~2.7× over). Caveat: only Q2 readable at runtime (BA283 = Blockwise path, TR1/TR2 in BlockwiseStage have no op-point accessor).

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
SMALL-SIGNAL .ac-STYLE GAIN MEASUREMENT (complements the transient-golden level measurement above). No engine logic changed — added one measurement test fn `ba283_small_signal_gain_sweep` (+ a Goertzel single-bin helper) in pedalkernel-validate/tests/neve1073_spice.rs. Branch combined-measure (= adapted-input-port a371b617 + merged main #181/#182/#183 servo). NOTE: origin/adapted-input-port no longer exists on remote; combined-measure IS the equivalent "both fixes" state (verified: a371b617 input-port + 4f0e41d3 #183 servo both present). Build green `cargo build -p pedalkernel --features diag` (22s). Disk OK, no ENOSPC (5.8→4.6 GB used incrementally).

METHOD: drive a SMALL sine, 0.5 s warmup (skip coupling-cap/servo transient), then realized gain = Goertzel fundamental at drive bin, output_amp/input_amp → dB. Gain control = 0.5 (design). SR 48k. PK_SERVO_ENABLE=1.

DELIVERABLE TABLE (drive = 2 mV peak, servo ON):
| freq   | SPICE .ac design | WDF realized | gap      |
|--------|------------------|--------------|----------|
| 100 Hz | +21.9 dB         | +0.1 dB      | -21.8 dB |
| 1 kHz  | +19.1 dB         | +0.1 dB      | -19.0 dB |
| 10 kHz | +3.3 dB          | +4.6 dB      | +1.3 dB  |

(1) AMPLITUDE + LINEARITY: 2 mV peak. Linearity VERIFIED — halving to 1 mV holds the dB gain (Δ ≤ 0.14 dB; out_amp ratio 0.508/0.502/0.499, ideal 0.500) at all three freqs. So at the small-signal operating point the stage is genuinely linear; the result is not a clipping/large-signal artifact.

(2) SHAPE: NO — the WDF does NOT match the SPICE rolloff scaled down. It's a DIFFERENT shape. SPICE design rolls OFF (21.9→19.1→3.3, ~-18 dB across the band). WDF is ~FLAT ≈0 dB at 100 Hz/1 kHz and RISES to +4.6 dB at 10 kHz — opposite slope. With servo OFF it's flat ~0 dB at all three freqs (the +4.6 dB HF bump is the only thing the servo adds). So the gap is NOT a constant scalar: -21.8 / -19.0 / +1.3 dB.

(3) BELOW UNITY? Essentially AT UNITY at the design Gain=0.5 small-signal point (~0 dB), not the ~-13 dB inferred and not actively attenuating. The active gain is collapsed: the +24 V Class-A block delivers ≈0 dB instead of its +19-22 dB design — ~19-22 dB short at LF.

RECONCILES with the transient measurement above: that read WDF_out 0.148 V vs golden_out 6.88 V = -33 dB LEVEL gap; golden realizes +39.7 dB (transient, large-signal) so WDF@0.1V = +6.4 dB. Small-signal (2 mV) is lower still (~0 dB) — gain falls as drive shrinks, i.e. the realized op-point gain is amplitude/basin dependent.

OP-POINT FRAGILITY (sanity probe, 1 kHz 2 mV, sweeping RU1 feedback pot): realized gain is NON-MONOTONIC and basin-sensitive — Gain=0.1→+2.2, 0.3→+1.6, 0.5→+0.1, 0.7→+25.5, 0.9→+12.1 dB. So the block is NOT a dead passthrough (it responds strongly to the feedback pot), but its DC operating point is mis-biased: at the design Gain=0.5 it lands in a near-unity basin; nudging to 0.7 jumps to +25 dB. This is the knife-edge conducting basin the servo STATUS note (general.rs:1869) describes. The unity-ish result at Gain=0.5 is a real mis-bias, not an artifact.

SHAKY/CAVEATS: (a) the +4.6 dB at 10 kHz is genuine but small and servo-dependent; (b) the Gain=0.5 unity result sits in a fragile basin — a different warmup/seed could land elsewhere (the pot sweep shows ±25 dB swings nearby), so treat ±a few dB as the confidence on the LF numbers; the QUALITATIVE verdict (≈unity, ~20 dB below .ac design at LF, wrong slope) is solid. (c) Compared against the task-supplied .ac design numbers — no .ac deck exists in-repo (the public deck is transient-only), so the design column is the external reference, not re-derived here.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: SWEEP RESULT (2mV, servo on, Gain=0.5): WDF realized gain +0.1dB @100Hz, +0.1dB @1k, +4.6dB @10k vs SPICE design +21.9/+19.1/+3.3. So NOT -13dB attenuating — it collapses to UNITY at the design point. THREE signatures: (1) ~unity at LF not +19dB design; (2) SHAPE INVERTED — design rolls OFF (-18dB across band), WDF RISES (+4.6 at 10k) — opposite slope; (3) gain NON-MONOTONIC vs feedback pot: 0.5->+0.1, 0.7->+25.5, 0.9->+12.1 dB (±25dB swings, near-oscillation at 0.7). => NOT a scalar gm×load collapse — it's a LOOP-DYNAMICS / reactive-feedback issue. The DC op-point is held (servo); the AC feedback loop is mis-phased. Rising-at-HF where design rolls off = compensation acting BACKWARDS (Cmil 220p Miller / Ccmp 330p / Cfb 4n7 wrong sign/coupling in the fused scattering). Non-monotonic-vs-pot = ill-conditioned closed loop. Knife-edge basin caveat: LF numbers ±few dB, qualitative verdict solid.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
CROSS-REFERENCE EXPERIMENT (xref-feedback branch) — engine-bug vs BA283-topology.

GOAL: build a MINIMAL, textbook, SPICE-faithful feedback amplifier in BOTH ngspice
and a WDF .pedal (identical nodes/values/2N3904 model) and compare small-signal
gain, to decide if the BA283 gain bug is an ENGINE feedback-path bug or a BA283
.pedal/topology bug. MEASUREMENT ONLY — no engine code changed. Build green
(pedalkernel + validate, --features diag). Disk OK, no ENOSPC.

ARTIFACTS (all public, committed on xref-feedback):
  spice-circuits/active/xref_feedback_amp.spice      (2-BJT shunt-feedback, templated Rf/Cf)
  spice-circuits/active/xref_twostage_nofb.spice     (control: same 2 stages, NO global fb)
  spice-circuits/active/xref_single_bjt_fb.spice     (bonus: 1-BJT collector->base fb)
  circuits/active/xref_feedback_amp.pedal            (faithful WDF twin)
  circuits/active/xref_twostage_nofb.pedal
  circuits/active/xref_single_bjt_fb.pedal
  tests/xref_feedback_amp.rs                         (WDF measurement: Goertzel gain, linearity, sweeps)
  tools/xref_spice_ac.sh                             (ngspice .op + .ac sweep helper)

REFERENCE CIRCUIT: two DC-coupled 2N3904 common-emitter stages, emitter-bypassed
for high open-loop gain, +24V rail, with GLOBAL shunt-shunt feedback out->Rf->Q1
base and a compensation cap Cf in parallel with Rf (the reactive port INSIDE the
loop). Rf also DC-biases Q1's base. Design point Rf=33k. ngspice DC op-point is
healthy (Q1/Q2 Ic~2mA, Vbe~0.69V, output mid-rail ~13.8V).

═══ TABLE: closed-loop gain (dB), SPICE .ac vs WDF, per freq, per Rf ═══

SPICE .ac (ground truth — trustworthy, faithful):
  2-stage shunt-fb     100Hz   1kHz   10kHz  100kHz
    Rf=15k             +9.76  +12.50  +12.54  +12.21
    Rf=22k            +12.99  +15.41  +15.43  +14.43
    Rf=33k (design)   +16.55  +18.69  +18.69  +16.23   <- +19dB passband, rolls OFF at HF
    Rf=47k            +19.64  +21.60  +21.54  +17.11
  2-stage NO fb              +82.8  +83.3  +83.3  +81.4   (huge open-loop gain)
  1-BJT C->B fb Rf=220k     +35.0  +35.1  +32.9  +16.8   (rolls off at HF)

WDF default compile (Blockwise, what compile_pedal gives for 2 DC-coupled BJTs):
  2-stage shunt-fb     100Hz   1kHz   10kHz  100kHz
    Rf=15k           -140.2  -140.2  -139.8  -140.2
    Rf=33k (design)  -139.7  -139.7  -139.2  -139.6   <- SILENCE (~ -140 dB)
  2-stage NO fb (Blockwise)        -123.7 dB @1k        <- also SILENCE, no fb needed
  1-BJT C->B fb Rf=220k     +39.3  +39.6  +38.2  +39.3  <- CORRECT magnitude, but flat (no HF rolloff)
  single CE (no fb, existing)      +36.3 dB @1k         <- CORRECT

WDF on the BA283's actual path (skip_blockwise -> MultiNl grouped-NR co-solve):
  2-stage NO fb (MultiNl)          -0.56 dB flat        <- collapses to ~UNITY (SPICE +83dB)
  2-stage shunt-fb     100Hz    1kHz   10kHz  100kHz
    Rf=15k            -7.91   -20.81  -46.37  -38.39
    Rf=22k           -17.90   -26.42  -46.28  -38.34
    Rf=33k (design)  +43.58   -26.25  -46.11  -14.39   <- design gives -26dB (SPICE +18.7); +43.6 spike @100Hz
    Rf=47k            -7.61   -26.12  -45.99  -38.10
  1kHz vs Rf = [-20.81, -26.42, -26.25, -26.12] -> NON-MONOTONIC (drops then flat)
  100Hz vs Rf = [-7.9, -17.9, +43.6, -7.6]      -> +/-50dB swing, near-oscillation spike at Rf=33k

═══ VERDICT: REPRODUCES the BA283 signature -> ENGINE bug in the feedback path ═══

The textbook, SPICE-faithful circuit reproduces ALL THREE BA283 signatures on the
SAME engine path the BA283 uses (MultiNl multi-BJT grouped-NR co-solve):

  1. CLOSED-LOOP GAIN COLLAPSES: design Rf=33k WDF = -26 dB @1k where SPICE = +18.7 dB
     (~45 dB deficit). The no-feedback MultiNl control already collapses to ~UNITY
     (-0.56 dB vs SPICE +83 dB) — the "unity-ish gain" signature, exactly as BA283.
  2. FREQUENCY SLOPE INVERTED / non-physical: SPICE rolls OFF with frequency; the WDF
     MultiNl response is non-monotonic in freq and HIGHER at 100kHz than 10kHz
     (rises at HF), with a +43.6 dB anomalous spike at 100Hz/Rf=33k.
  3. NON-MONOTONIC vs FEEDBACK: SPICE gain is cleanly monotonic-increasing with Rf
     (+12.5 -> +21.6 dB). The WDF MultiNl is NON-monotonic, with a +/-50 dB swing and
     a near-oscillation spike at one Rf setting (100Hz column) — exactly the BA283
     "+/-25 dB non-monotonic, near-oscillation at one setting" signature.

PATH-SPECIFICITY (key for the fix):
  * SINGLE-BJT path (WDF root, single-BJT C->B feedback AND plain CE) is CORRECT in
    magnitude: +39.6 / +36.3 dB, matching SPICE +35 / (open-loop). The single-BJT
    feedback root handles feedback fine. (Caveat: single-BJT WDF does NOT show the
    SPICE HF rolloff — stays flat to 100kHz — a milder reactive-port-in-loop issue,
    but gain is right.)
  * MULTI-BJT MultiNl path is where the dramatic signature appears — co-solved 2-BJT
    group with a global loop. The bug is on the grouped-NR / multi-BJT co-solve path,
    NOT the single-BJT root.
  * The DEFAULT Blockwise path (chained NL blocks) collapses to SILENCE (-140 dB)
    even WITHOUT feedback — a third, distinct breakage in the DC-coupled multi-BJT
    cascade. So the multi-BJT compile paths (both Blockwise and MultiNl) are broken
    for DC-coupled cascades; the single-BJT root is the only one that works.

CONCLUSION: this is an ENGINE bug in the multi-BJT (grouped-NR / co-solved) path,
INDEPENDENT of BA283 topology. The bug is triggered by two DC-coupled BJTs co-solved
as a group (the collapse appears even with NO feedback on the MultiNl path), and the
global feedback loop on top adds the inverted-slope / non-monotonic-vs-feedback /
near-oscillation behavior. BA283's .pedal is NOT the prime suspect — a textbook,
component-faithful circuit fails identically. The BA283 .pedal faithfully models its
circuit; the engine's coupled-BJT solve is what's wrong.

WHAT TO RE-EXAMINE (engine, not the .pedal):
  - The grouped-NR multi-BJT co-solve (MultiNl / blockwise inter-block coupling): the
    no-feedback 2-BJT cascade losing ~83 dB of gain to ~unity means the inter-stage
    transconductance coupling is being lost / mis-scattered, consistent with the
    a/2Rp Norton-source-vs-port-current confusion noted in MEMORY (WDF NR convention)
    and the input-port r_adapted=1000 hardcode (this bead). The feedback loop then
    rides on top of an already-collapsed open-loop gain.
  - The reactive-port-in-feedback sign/phase (the +43.6dB 100Hz spike + HF rise) is a
    SECONDARY effect once the loop is closed around the broken co-solve.

NOTE: this experiment is consistent with the working hypothesis (reactive cap in a
fused-scattering feedback loop mishandled) but REFINES it: the primary defect is the
multi-BJT co-solved open-loop gain collapse; the reactive-port-in-loop phase error is
the secondary frequency/feedback-shape distortion layered on top.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: CROSS-REFERENCE = DECISIVE: ENGINE bug, NOT BA283 topology. Built a textbook 2-BJT shunt-feedback amp FAITHFULLY in both ngspice + WDF .pedal (identical nodes/values/2N3904 model). RESULTS (1kHz): single-BJT (WDF-root path) CORRECT (+36/+40 vs SPICE +35 ✓). MULTI-BJT (MultiNl) BROKEN: 2-stage NO-feedback SPICE +83.3dB vs WDF -0.56dB; 2-stage +feedback SPICE +18.7 vs WDF -26.3. Blockwise path = silence (-140dB). KEY: the bug appears WITHOUT feedback — a 2-BJT CASCADE loses ~84dB to unity. So the PRIMARY defect is INTER-STAGE GAIN COLLAPSE in the multi-BJT co-solve (the grouped-NR/MultiNl scattering loses the gain between co-solved BJTs), NOT the feedback caps (corrects the prior reactive-cap hypothesis — feedback only layers inverted-slope/non-monotonic on top). Single-BJT root path is FINE. MINIMAL REPRODUCER preserved on origin/xref-feedback: xref_twostage_nofb.pedal (+83 design -> unity WDF). Fix target = MultiNl multi-port inter-stage scattering. BA283 topology EXONERATED.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
DISSECTION: where the inter-stage gain dies in the multi-BJT MultiNl scattering (branch dissect-interstage, off xref-feedback). EMPIRICAL-FIRST, no engine logic changed — added only #[cfg(feature=\"debug-trace\")] per-port dumps (steady-state-gated via PK_TRACE_SKIP) + 4 measurement tests + feature wiring.

== SPICE GROUND TRUTH (ngspice .ac, v_in=1V) ==
xref_twostage_nofb:  nb1=-6.5dB | nc1(Q1 collector, inter-stage)=+33.8dB | nout=+83.3dB. Both stages amplify; nc1==nb2 DC-coupled lossless. DC op-pt healthy (nb1=2.72 nc1=3.58 nout=10.5V).
xref_single_bjt_fb:  +35.1dB @1k (the WORKING reference).

== WDF REPRODUCTION (96k, amp=0.01, 1kHz) ==
single CE (Blockwise):              +36.3dB  OK
two-stage NOFB (default=Blockwise): -123.7dB BROKEN
two-stage NOFB (skip_blockwise):    -0.56dB  BROKEN (unity)
two-stage SHUNT FB (MultiNl):       -26.3dB  BROKEN
single-BJT C->B FB (MultiNl):       +39.6dB  OK (reference)

== KEY STRUCTURAL FINDING: the circuits take DIFFERENT engine paths ==
- xref_single_bjt_fb -> 1 MultiNlStage [BjtNpn2P] n_nl=2  -> WORKS
- xref_twostage_nofb default -> 1 BlockwiseStage (2 BJT blocks, 6 ports) + 1 WDF buffer. The Blockwise BJT ladder ATTENUATES (PIPE in=6.54e-4 -> post-block 7.29e-5, ~ -19dB) -> -123dB.
- xref_twostage_nofb skip_blockwise -> 7 chained PASSIVE WdfStages, root_comp_id EMPTY, mnl=0: the BJTs are DROPPED to passive, signal passes unity (-0.56dB).
- xref_feedback_amp (global Rf loop) -> 1 MultiNlStage [BjtNpn2P,BjtNpn2P] n_nl=4 + 1 WDF buffer. THIS is the BA283 grouped-NR path. BROKEN.
So the genuine multi-BJT MultiNl group is built ONLY by the FEEDBACK topology (the loop can't be split into a forward ladder). That n_nl=4 grouped solve is the core bug.

== PER-NODE / PER-PORT TRACE (steady state) ==
Port order for 2-BJT cascade = [Q1.Vbe, Q1.Vce(=nc1), Q2.Vbe(=nc1), Q2.Vce(=nout)] (general.rs:514-517).

WORKING single-BJT [BjtNpn2P] n_nl=2:
  NR iters = 1-3 (CONVERGES), 0 NR-diag(>100) hits.
  v_port=[0.6977(Vbe forward), 3.94(Vce active, swinging)]  Rp=[1000, 2818]
  s_nl rows: [-0.0198, 0.021 / 0.059, 0.0]  s_nl_adapted=[0.98, 0.059]  -> gain +66dB instantaneous.

BROKEN 2-BJT feedback [BjtNpn2P,BjtNpn2P] n_nl=4:
  NR iters = 24 (HARD CAP) on 100% of samples -> NEVER CONVERGES. iter0_residual ~121.
  Seed (q-point homotopy) is CORRECT: iter0 v=[0.784, 0.335, 0.649, 11.0] (Q1.Vbe fwd, Q2.Vce active).
  But NR DIVERGES away from the good seed to the clamp rails:
    final v_port=[-0.78401(Q1.Vbe REVERSE, =-vbe_max clamp), 22.07, 0.78, -24.00000(Q2.Vce = -v_max clamp)].
    Q1 ends reverse-biased, Q2 railed; output is clamp noise -> -26dB.
  Rp=[153.9, 2652, 15317, 153.9]  <-- the Vbe ports (0,3) COLLAPSED to 153.9 ohm (vs 1000 in the working single BJT).
  s_nl rows:
    row0 Q1.Vbe = [-0.078, 0.000, 0.000, 0.922]
    row1 Q1.Vce = [0.000, 0.043, 0.093, -0.000]
    row2 Q2.Vbe = [-0.000, 0.535, 0.022, 0.000]  <- inter-stage coupling Q1.Vce->Q2.Vbe = 0.535 (PRESENT, not lost)
    row3 Q2.Vce = [0.922, -0.000, 0.000, -0.078]  <- global FB Rf coupling Q1.Vbe<->Q2.Vce = 0.922 (PRESENT)
  known_a (steady) = [14.5, 21.4, -7.06, -12.7] (HUGE; single-BJT was ~[0.85,13.4]); b_passive=[2.79,8.38,7.25,-5.67] huge.

ANSWER TO THE FORK: It is NEITHER \"stage-1 collapses at the port\" NOR \"coupling loses it.\" The inter-stage off-diagonal coupling (s_nl[2][1]=0.535) and the feedback coupling (s_nl[0][3]=0.922) are BOTH structurally present with sane magnitude/sign. The gain dies because the n_nl=4 grouped Newton-Raphson FAILS TO CONVERGE (24-iter cap every sample) and the iterate runs from a correct seed to the Vbe/Vce clamp rails. The two BJTs end up decoupled garbage.

== CODE MECHANISM (file:line) ==
1) ROOT TRIGGER — iterative Thevenin adaptation, general.rs:919-950 (derive_scattering).
   Loop: z_th = Rp_i*(1+s_refl)/(1-s_refl) for s_refl=s_nl[i][i]. The Vbe self-reflection is NEGATIVE (s_nl_diag[0]=-0.078 for the 4-port vs -0.0198 for the single). Negative s_refl => factor (1+s)/(1-s)<1 => Rp SHRINKS every iter, monotonically collapsing the Vbe port resistance 1000 -> 153.9 ohm in 5 iters WITHOUT settling. The single-BJT Vbe stays ~1000 (weaker negative s_refl, adaptation barely moves). The collapsed Rp makes the Jacobian term Rp*di_be/dv = Rp*gm extremely stiff for the exponential base junction, and the cross-coupled off-diagonals (solver.rs:1008-1014, s_nl[i][j]*Rp_j*dij_dvk) compound it -> the damped Newton (solver.rs:920-1057) overshoots to the clamps.
2) SYMPTOM SITE — grouped NR, solver.rs:920-1057 (multi_port_nr_solve_grouped_into): residual F_i = known_a[i] - a_i + sum s_nl[i][j]*b_j (962-968); clamp at 926-933 + v_clamp_port (bjt.rs: Vbe->+-vbe_max, Vce->+-v_max) pins the diverged iterate at the rails; iters_used hits NR_MAX_ITER=24.
3) NOTE: the DC q-point homotopy seed (general.rs:334-345 solve_bjt_group_dc_qpoint / apply_bjt_dc_qpoint) is WORKING (iter0 seed is the correct conducting op-pt). The bug is downstream: the per-sample WDF scattering+NR cannot stay there.

== FIX DIRECTION (NOT implemented — investigation only) ==
Primary suspect: the Thevenin adaptation (general.rs:919-950) is unsafe for tightly-coupled multi-BJT groups — it collapses negative-self-reflection conducting-junction ports to unphysically low Rp, producing a stiff, non-convergent grouped-NR. Candidate directions, in order of confidence:
  (a) HIGH confidence the adaptation is the trigger: gate/clamp it for multi-NL conducting ports (don't shrink Rp below the device's small-signal port resistance; or skip adaptation when |s_refl| would drive Rp down past a floor; or only adapt when it RAISES Rp). Re-measure: does the 4-port then converge like the 2-port?
  (b) MED: improve grouped-NR robustness for stiff coupled exponential junctions (line search / Rp-scaled damping / source-stepping homotopy at audio rate) so it tolerates the adapted Rp.
  (c) LOWER/INDEPENDENT: the OTHER two failing paths are separate defects to file — Blockwise 2-BJT ladder attenuates (-123dB), and skip_blockwise drops BJTs to passive (mnl=0, -0.56dB). These are NOT the MultiNl grouped-NR bug; they are stage-selection/Blockwise issues.

STILL UNCERTAIN: whether fixing the adaptation alone restores full +83/+19dB or whether the grouped-NR also needs damping hardening; and whether s_refl=-0.078 is itself an artifact of a mis-signed port-current/Norton convention in the 4-port MNA-derived scattering (the bead-noted VCC/Norton confusion) vs a legitimate negative reflection. Next step before any fix: experimentally pin Rp_Vbe=1000 (disable adaptation) for the 4-port and re-run the iters/gain trace to confirm convergence is restored.

Repro: branch dissect-interstage; cargo test -p pedalkernel-validate --features debug-trace --test xref_feedback_amp xref_dump_feedback_multinl -- --nocapture --test-threads=1 (PK_TRACE_SKIP=2000). Companion: xref_dump_single_bjt (working). DISK was tight (~270MB low water mark); no cargo clean used.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
ADAPTATION-FLOOR EXPERIMENT (branch adaptation-floor off dissect-interstage 151d6656) — ROOT CAUSE NOT CONFIRMED; the dissection's hypothesis is DISCONFIRMED.

STEP 1 result. Added a gated experiment in rigid/general.rs derive_scattering (PK_PIN_NL_RP: "off"=baseline default, "floor"=never shrink NL port below init, "pin"=hard-pin NL ports to init 1000). Measured the n_nl=4 MultiNl feedback group (xref_feedback_amp, skip_blockwise) with a new NR-stats probe (pedalkernel-validate/tests/xref_nr_probe.rs: NR iters + clamp/cap + gain) and PK_RP_TRACE (final NL Rp + s_diag). 1kHz, amp=0.01, 96k.

NR convergence + gain per mode (feedback amp, grouped-NR n_nl=4):
  mode=off (baseline):
    Rf=15k gain -20.81  avg_iter 1.33  cap_hits 1600   resid 9.8e-5  (CONVERGES)
    Rf=22k gain -26.42  avg_iter 24.0  cap_hits 9600   resid 3.98    (DIVERGES, 24-cap 100%)
    Rf=33k gain -26.25  avg_iter 24.0  cap_hits 9600   resid 3.95
    Rf=47k gain -26.12  avg_iter 24.0  cap_hits 9600   resid 3.94
  mode=pin (Rp pinned 1000):
    Rf=15k gain -20.92  avg_iter 24.0  cap_hits 9600   resid 29.9   (now DIVERGES — WORSE than off)
    Rf=33k gain -20.99  avg_iter 24.0  resid 29.97
  mode=floor:
    Rf=33k gain -22.66  avg_iter 24.0  cap_hits 9600   resid 10.5   (monotonic vs Rf=true, but still diverges)

CONCLUSION: pinning/flooring Rp does NOT restore convergence and does NOT restore gain (stays ~-21..-23 dB, target +18.7 dB). It makes things WORSE: off-mode Rf=15k actually converged (avg 1.33 iters); pin-mode makes ALL Rf hit the 24-iter cap with residual ~30.

WHY the hypothesis is inverted (PK_RP_TRACE, n_nl=4 Vbe ports 0,3):
  off:   nl_rp[Vbe]=153.9   s_diag[Vbe]=-0.078   (small reflection — well matched)
  pin:   nl_rp[Vbe]=1000    s_diag[Vbe]=-0.355   (BADLY mismatched)
  floor: nl_rp[Vbe]=1000    s_diag[Vbe]=-0.355
The Thevenin adaptation collapsing Rp 1000->153.9 is the adaptation CORRECTLY matching the port (driving s_refl toward 0). The negative s_refl is NOT caused by a small Rp; it is what the UNADAPTED 1000-ohm port reflects, and the adaptation shrinks Rp to fix it. So "Rp shrink -> divergence" is backwards. Pinning Rp re-creates the mismatch and diverges harder.

There is NO line search / monotone-residual backtracking, so a full Newton step on the stiff coupled junctions overshoots to the rails. This matches the dissection's lower-confidence candidate (b), not (a). known_a at the Vbe ports is huge (~14-21 per dissection) — worth a separate check for a source-term/Norton-convention scale issue in the MNA-derived scattering, but the immediate failure is NR robustness.

title: Runtime-hold fix: low-rate, physics-derived DC re-solve/servo for SignalPath feedback servos (close BA283)
description: PROVEN (3hsi/paky/ej0v): BA283's -49.5dB is the deep-WDF runtime-hold — the CONDUCTING op-point is an exact single-step fixed point (apply_dc_qpoint_seed, sign-confirmed) but unstable in the local per-sample cap-coupled dynamics, so the runtime slides to the STARVED fixed point (2N3055 7uA vs SPICE 218uA). Bias computation, sign, convention, mapping ALL ruled out. FIX: replicate what SPICE does (re-solve the global DC equilibrium) but at the rate the bias PHYSICALLY moves, not per-sample. (1) PHYSICS-DERIVED RATE at compile time: tau = R_thevenin x C per reactive element (REUSE r_control_thevenin machinery + comp.kind.capacitance(); reactive_precharge already has cap DC), dominant tau over the servo group => correction bandwidth ~1/(2*pi*tau), re-solve interval << tau. NOT a hardcoded constant. (2) RUNTIME: low-rate global DC re-solve to the CONDUCTING op-point (use bias.rs nodal solve ~0.608, NOT the wave-domain joint solve which finds cutoff) + re-pin dc_bias via apply_dc_qpoint_seed; OR a continuous leaky DC-servo (stabilizing integral correction, like the real analog servo) at bandwidth 1/tau. (3) GATE to SignalPath feedback servos only (the #182/classifier topology); leave StaticBias/op-amp circuits untouched. SUCCESS: BA283 ~0dB, 2N3055 runtime Ic 7uA->~218uA (verify via diag --tail #182), no golden regression. If it can't close cleanly: gate off + report.

title: Introduce a shared OnePort type for port-voltage state + the WDF port-wave convention, across all stage types
description: Today port state + the port-wave conventions are SPLIT: each stage type (Wdf/MultiNl/Iir/StateSpace/Blockwise) stores its own port info; NlDeviceIv (solver.rs:340) gives only i(v); the grouped-NR solver does the a/b/Rp/Norton mapping; explicit single-diodes (diode.rs:779) do their OWN port-wave math. This split is the root of the port-current/Norton convention drift (the BA283 31dB loop-gain deficit, paky). DESIGN (user): one OnePort type holding port-voltage info (v/a/b, port resistance Rp) + the canonical sign + Norton/port-current mapping (I_port = a/(2Rp) + i_device; b from i_device), SHARED by all stage types. Device impls provide only i(v); the OnePort applies the universal convention once, correctly. Sequence AFTER paky proves the correct convention (so we house the right math, not the wrong one) and after #163/#173 merge (quiet tree). Big blast radius - deliberate campaign, gate on full golden suite.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: DIRECTIVE (user): ONE single definition of voltage/wave, shared by ALL stages — DRY is how we nip engine bugs in the bud. The 31dB loop-gain drift (paky) is the proof: it's a convention duplicated across TWO parallel port-state systems that desynced — OnePort/WdfWaveCache (boundary_math.rs, MNA/boundary/reactive path) vs DynNode/WdfLeaf (the WDF tree's per-leaf state). SCOPE (not 'bridge the two' — CONVERGE to one): the canonical voltage/wave = OnePort<N> + WdfWaveCache (wave_state/previous_reflected) + the typed PortVoltage/IncidentWave/ReflectedWave wrappers (already exist, boundary_math.rs:81-409). Adopt it EVERYWHERE: the WDF tree (DynNode/WdfLeaf -> OnePort, retire WdfLeaf's ad-hoc voltage state) AND the grouped-NR port-wave AND all stage types. The sign + Norton/port-current mapping = ONE canonical impl on that type (so no path can drift). This PREVENTS the whole convention-drift bug class. Big blast radius - deliberate campaign on a quiet tree, AFTER paky proves the correct convention + #163/#173 merge. paky is the tactical proof+close; zekh is the structural cure.
