title: BA283 last 31dB: fix the WDF-NR loop-gain deficit (Norton/port-current convention in the port-wave layer)
description: b2ps: DC op-point correct+stable, shape matches, but MultiNl small-signal LOOP gain is -3.34dB vs +39.76dB needed (~31dB / ~300x deficit, = 685e). The port-wave math is SPLIT: NlDeviceIv (solver.rs:340) gives only i(v); the grouped-NR solver does the a/b/Rp port mapping for NlDeviceGroupIv; explicit single-diodes do their OWN Wright-omega port-wave (diode.rs:779). NO unified OnePort port adapter. Prime suspect (NR-solver-convention memo): the grouped-NR confuses DEVICE current with PORT current (b=-2Rp*i_device vs I_port=a/(2Rp)+i_device, the Norton source term a/(2Rp)) -> loop gain deficient. FIX: unify the port-wave convention (sign + Norton/port-current) into ONE shared layer so the grouped-NR realizes the full loop gain, consistent with the working single-port path. Verify via diag ring (PK_JOINTDC op-point underneath): BA283 -31.9->~0, MultiNl gain -> +39.76dB, stable. BLAST RADIUS: ALL NL devices (grouped-NR) - gate on full golden suite, tb303 excluded.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
DISPROVEN: the grouped-NR port-current/Norton convention is NOT the BA283 gain deficit. Branch paky-norton-portcurrent (off b2ps-generic-dc-qpoint + merged origin/main 451af5cb; worktree .claude/worktrees/agent-a17ecd698fac6e70c). NO code change shipped (Rule 1).

WHAT I TESTED (the prime suspect, exactly as briefed): implemented the doubled-wave convention in multi_port_nr_solve_grouped_into (residual + Jacobian + reflected wave + frozen-cache path), gated PK_NORTON_DOUBLED (default off, byte-identical verified: gate-off BA283 = 0.0229V / -49.5 dB exactly). The change makes the grouped solver agree with the single-port newton_raphson_solve reference (verified numerically: for an isolated NL port, doubled grouped == single-port == textbook one-port b=a-2R*i; standard grouped differs by the Norton term a/2R).

RESULT — the doubled convention makes BA283 WORSE, not better:
  baseline (gate off):           -49.5 dB
  PK_JOINTDC=1 (b2ps seed):      -31.9 dB
  PK_NORTON_DOUBLED=1 alone:     -55.9 dB  (THD err 79.7 dB)  <- WORSE
  PK_NORTON_DOUBLED + JOINTDC:   -52.8 dB  (THD err 79.1 dB)  <- WORSE
=> reverted the change.

WHY the convention is NOT the bug: the single-port WDF roots (diode.rs explicit_diode_pair) use a DOUBLED-wave tree (a = 2*standard, root solves v+Rp*i = a/2). The grouped MultiNl uses an MNA-derived R-type scattering S where a = S*b in the STANDARD half-wave convention (a=v+R*i, b=v-R*i). Each subsystem is internally self-consistent with its OWN known_a scale; they do NOT share one 'a'. Imposing the diode-tree doubled convention on the R-type grouped solver is wrong -> worsens. The grouped solver's known_a = S_passive*b_passive + S_adapted*b_adapted + dc_bias already carries the proper source term; no Norton term is dropped.

THE REAL MECHANISM (measured via ba283_runtime_nr diag ring, PK_JOINTDC=1, --features diag): the grouped NR converges (max_resid 1.7e-5) and transconductance IS applied correctly (grp0 dIc/(gm*dVbe)=0.983). The joint-DC fixed point holds v* = [TR1 Vbe=0.402 Vce=19.18, TR2 Vbe=0.536 Vce=18.78, TR3 Vbe=0.608 Vce=5.37]. TR1 (input stage) is STARVED at Vbe=0.402 (gm=0.0013, ~30x below a conducting Si BJT) -> the input stage delivers ~no gain -> the -31 dB deficit. (NB: b2ps's '-49->-31, TR1 Vbe=0.606 held' read TR3, not TR1; the input TR1 is held at 0.402 in the converged v*.)

ROOT: the wave-domain DC fixed point (dc_bias as NR known_a on NL ports + vcc_bias_all post-scatter on ALL ports) is self-consistent (walk-off=0, cap-err 1e-10) but biases TR1 near cutoff -- it is NOT the nodal SPICE operating point (TR1 wants Vbe~0.65, Ic in mA). = exactly b2ps's own remaining residual + 685e's final verdict + y2wj. This is the ko5g DC-bias workstream (main just merged compiler/bias.rs, the unified BiasSeed core), NOT the grouped-NR port-wave layer.

RECOMMEND: close/redirect paky -> the fix is making dc_bias + vcc_bias_all rail-consistent so the wave-domain DC fixed point equals the nodal op-point (TR1 conducts), via the new compiler/bias.rs core, with the grouped-NR convention left as-is (it is correct). The grouped-NR port-current/Norton convention is verified correct and is NOT the lever.

GATE 2 (no-regression): trivially PASS -- branch carries NO code change vs b2ps+main (convention experiment reverted). Gate-off BA283 byte-identical (0.0229V). Lib baseline on this branch: 941 passed / 181 failed (== documented pre-existing baseline exactly). Build green (cargo build -p pedalkernel --features diag, pedalkernel-rt). Left in_progress, no PR.

comments.text: CONVENTION DISPROVEN (no code shipped, Rule 1). Implemented the doubled-wave/Norton convention in multi_port_nr_solve_grouped (PK_NORTON_DOUBLED): BA283 -49.5->-55.9dB WORSE (THD 79.7). REVERTED. comments.text: SIGN CONVENTION CONFIRMED CORRECT (read-only check, origin/main). Grouped-NR residual (solver.rs ~877): fi = known_a[i] - v_guess[i] - port_resistances[i]*cached_currents[i] => at convergence known_a = v + Rp*i, i = eval device current. apply_dc_qpoint_seed builds known_a = v* + Rp*i(v*) - Σ s_ij*(v*_j - Rp_j*i_j) [=Σ s_ij*b_j] — SAME convention, same sign, ×1 Rp factor (the ×2 was the single-diode doubled-wave path, not this grouped one). title: BA283 closure: stabilize the joint NL-port + reactive-port DC equilibrium (deep-WDF cosolve)
description: g725.2 injects TR1's correct DC operating point (Vbe 0.36->0.608, exact NR fixed point) -> 18dB recovered (-49.5->-31.4dB), but UNSTABLE: holding the BJT op-point makes the grouped NR + the reactive NFB caps a JOINT equilibrium the static seed doesn't stabilize -> caps drift, NR residual ~27, diverges. The remaining ~31dB + the instability = the deep-WDF cosolve: the DC seed must be a STABLE joint fixed point of the NL devices AND the reactive-port DC charge (consistent cap pre-charge + the feedback-loop dynamics), not a static per-port seed. = the long-banked engine-adapted-input-port-impedance / cosolve family. INVESTIGATE (empirically, via the diag runtime ring with PK_BJT_DCQPOINT=1): watch the caps + BJTs settle vs drift, find why the joint equilibrium isn't stable (cap DC state vs the BJT op-point; per-sample feedback drift). Then propose the deep-WDF fix. Tooling: g725.2-bjt-dc-qpoint branch + pedalkernel diag --tail.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: REFRAME (architecture): the fix is NOT 'stabilize g725.2's static per-type seed' — it's make the DC Q-point GENERIC + trait-based. Runtime is ALREADY generic (NlDeviceGroupIv trait + multi_port_nr_solve_grouped co-solves any group); only the DC Q-point is hardcoded per-type (compute_triode_dc_qpoint = single-triode-only + reimplements; g725.2 compute_bjt_dc_qpoint = parallel copy). DESIGN: one compute_group_dc_qpoint that runs the runtime's OWN grouped-NR over the group's &dyn NlDeviceGroupIv at DC. WHY it stabilizes: g725.2's seed is a fixed point of a SEPARATE Newton, not of multi_port_nr_solve_grouped -> drifts. Running the SAME solver at DC makes the seed a fixed point of the exact system the runtime iterates = consistent = stable. Retires the per-type triode/bjt/fet qpoint solvers. THE REAL WORK: reactive ports at DC (hold caps at the DC charge consistent with the op-point = the joint NL+reactive equilibrium) — but generic, solved once in the shared solver, not per-device. Replaces the per-type approach entirely.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
BASELINE NUMBERS (this worktree, build green w/ diag):
GOLDEN gate OFF: WDF RMS 0.0229V, -49.5 dB gap (byte-identical to established baseline). Diag ring TR1(g0) Vbe=0.362 gm=0.00028 (cutoff, ~120x low) — confirmed.
GATED ON (PK_BJT_DCQPOINT=1) diag ring — UNSTABLE, decays:
  block0 gain=193x (+45.7dB, OVERSHOOTS the 97x target), max_resid=3.87e5
  then gain DECAYS monotonically every block: 193->164->144->122->99->85->71->56->46... (out_rms halves ~every 2 blocks = exponential cap discharge), max_resid pinned at 27.45 (NR never re-converges).
  TR1(g0) Vbe=0.485 gm=0.0315 (recovered!), BUT TR2(g1) Vbe=-0.764 Ic~0 (CUTOFF/wrong), TR3(g2) Vce=-24.0 (rail-pinned/saturated).
MECHANISM CONFIRMED: the g725.2 seed is a fixed point of the NR SUB-problem (self-check max|F|~9e-16, NR-domain only) but NOT of the FULL runtime DC step (NR + scatter_all + post-scatter vcc_bias_all injection + cap unit-delay feedback): full-step residual = 27. The caps satisfy b_passive=a_prev (unit delay); at the seed a_passive != b_passive, so wdf_set_incident writes a different value each sample -> caps drift -> op-point collapses. Also the DC-solve node->port mapping mislabels g1/g2 vs runtime (g1 lands inverted).
DESIGN: generic compute_group_dc_qpoint must solve the JOINT fixed point of the FULL runtime DC step (input=0, dc_scale=1), enforcing cap steady-state a_passive[k]=b_passive[k] under the stage's OWN scattering+vcc_bias_all, so the seed is a true fixed point of what the runtime iterates.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
JOINT SOLVER v1 (PK_JOINTDC=1, solve_joint_dc_qpoint in stage.rs): the build-time relaxation of the full runtime DC step CONVERGES cleanly (nr_resid~1e-11, max_db 7e-1 -> 1.5e-7 over 256 iters) to a joint fixed point. BUT runtime still decays (gain 43->36->32->27->22... halving ~every 2 blocks) and the runtime op-point (g0 Vbe=-0.615, g2 Vbe=-0.764, g1 Vbe=0.652) does NOT match my converged seed (v[0]=0.051). 
ROOT FINDING: the wave-domain DC system the runtime iterates (known_a from dc_bias + post-scatter vcc_bias_all injection on ALL ports + cap unit-delay feedback) has a fixed point that is NOT the nonlinear NODAL solution (TR1 Vbe=0.608). My relaxation faithfully finds the wave-domain system's OWN fixed point, but that point is wrong/unstable because dc_bias (NR known_a, NL ports) and vcc_bias_all (post-scatter, ALL ports) encode the VCC/GND rails in two INCONSISTENT linear-superposition forms for a feedback topology -> the joint wave-domain DC fixed point != the true nodal operating point, and it's a decaying mode. block0 max_resid=3.87e5 (first-sample NR blowup, same as gated-ON). 
=> The fix can't just re-seed the existing wave-domain DC system; the DC SOURCE TERMS themselves (dc_bias + vcc_bias_all) must be made consistent with the nodal operating point so the wave-domain fixed point IS the nodal one. Investigating dc_bias vs vcc_bias_all rail encoding next.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
MILESTONE (commit, PK_JOINTDC gate): generic joint solver WORKS for stability. solve_joint_dc_qpoint(MultiNlStage) holds v* fixed (nodal Q-point), solves cap fixed point b_passive=a_passive under the stage's OWN scatter_all+vcc_bias_all, inverts dc_bias for the NR. VERIFIED a true fixed point: per-sample NR walk-off=0, cap-consistency err=1e-10. CRITICAL wiring fix: set_control(Gain=0.5) triggers recompute_scattering which REBUILDS scattering+dc_bias+vcc_bias_all and called apply_dc_qpoint_seed (g725.2 partial) -> destroyed the joint seed. Now recompute re-runs solve_joint_dc_qpoint against the NEW scattering when dc_qpoint_joint.
RESULT: op-point now CORRECT + HELD (TR1 Vbe=0.606, TR3 Vbe=0.401, NR converges every sample max_resid 1.7e-5 — vs g725.2's residual~27 divergent). Golden -49.5 -> -31.9 dB (RMS 0.0229->0.1747V, +17.6dB), shape MATCHES (norm RMS err -0.2dB, THD err 2.4dB). Default OFF byte-identical (0.0229V).
REMAINING (the real residual): with the op-point STABLE, a SLOW reactive mode still bleeds AC gain down: gain 188x(block0)->~11x(transient bump ~block30)->0.66x(block200,~530ms) monotone toward ~unity, out_rms 13->0.05. Op-point Vbe held throughout (resid 1.7e-5), so it's NOT op-point drift — a reactive DOF (cap Cfb 4n7 AC-feedback, or external Cin/Cout 10uF coupling Wdf stages) whose DC charge my seed doesn't perfectly match is slowly relaxing and dragging the closed-loop gain. The golden's short 480-sample trim catches the early high-gain part (-31.9dB); true steady state is worse. INVESTIGATING the slow mode source.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
LOCALIZATION (BA283_LEVELS probe under PK_JOINTDC, settled window): chain = input -> stage0(Wdf Cin) -> stage1(MultiNl) -> stage2(Wdf Cout) -> output.
  input->stage0(Cin): +0.00 dB (unity)
  stage0->stage1(MultiNl): -3.34 dB  (was -9.78 dB baseline => joint seed recovered ~6.4 dB of MultiNl gain)
  stage1->stage2(Cout): +11.89 dB (cap can't amplify -> this is the slow Cout DC-discharge transient inflating RMS in the window)
  realized chain gain 2.68x (+8.56 dB) vs golden 97x (+39.76 dB).
REFRAME: the MultiNl internal caps are STABLE (v_cap_leaf steady), op-point Vbe HELD (TR1 0.606), NR converges (resid 1.7e-5) — the JOINT DC EQUILIBRIUM IS STABILIZED (the bead's core ask). But the MultiNl's SETTLED small-signal gain is only -3.34 dB where the BA283 closed-loop gain must be ~+39.76 dB (Cin/Cout unity). The op-point CURRENTS are ~10x low: TR1 gm=0.0048 (Ic=120uA) where a properly-biased BC184C at Vbe=0.606 wants Ic~mA, gm~0.04. So Vbe is right but Ic/gm ~10x low -> small-signal gain ~20-40 dB low.
=> The remaining ~31 dB is the IN-MATRIX / SMALL-SIGNAL-GAIN deficit (= 685e's 'MultiNl realizes ~300x too little gain' verdict + MEMORY.md's WDF-NR Norton/port-vs-device-current convention), NOT the DC equilibrium. My work converts the UNSTABLE g725.2 partial into a STABLE op-point and recovers ~6 dB, but full ~97x closure needs the per-sample NR Jacobian/scattering gain fix, which is a distinct workstream. The early diag-ring gain=188x was the Cout-discharge transient, not steady gain. Assessing gate strategy per Rule 1.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:

title: BA283 gain fix: trace why TR1 runtime operating point settles at 0.36V vs computed 0.64V (dc_bias injection)
description: Phase B (runtime ring) measured: BA283 -49.5dB = DC operating-point bug. Input TR1 settles near cutoff at runtime Vbe=0.36V (bias_analysis computes/validates ~0.64V), Ic=7uA, gm 120x low -> no input-stage gain. Convergence healthy, transconductance exact, output Darlington correctly biased. The computed DC bias is right but NOT HELD in the runtime MultiNl grouped-NR. TRACE: the dc_bias VCC source-term / R2 56k base-bias injection path into TR1's base in the grouped-NR -> why does the NR settle TR1 at 0.36 not 0.64? Use the diag runtime ring (pedalkernel diag --tail) to watch it. Converges with the ko5g bias epic (g725) - the runtime dc_bias injection.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
MECHANISM FOUND (y2wj-tr1-bias-trace, runtime ring + dc_bias dump). WHY TR1 settles at 0.36V not 0.64V:

THE BIAS-INJECTION PATH. At runtime the MultiNl grouped-NR gets its DC operating point from ONE per-port DC source term: dc_bias[i], added into known_a[i] in MultiNlStage::process (pedalkernel-rt/src/stage.rs:6047-6065, a_i += dc * dc_scale). dc_bias is computed by compute_dc_bias() (pedalkernel/src/compiler/rigid/general.rs:896-949) as dc_bias[i] = vcc_injection[i] * supply_voltage, where vcc_injection comes from derive_scattering_and_vs_injection() (general.rs:844-849). That injection vector is a SINGLE LINEAR MNA solve: every BJT is replaced by its fixed linearized port resistance and only the VCC voltage source drives the network. It is pure linear superposition of the supply — it does NOT model the nonlinear DC-coupled feedback servo.

THE WRONG TERM (measured). PK9XU1_DEBUG dc_bias dump, port order [G0.be,G0.ce,G1.be,G1.ce,G2.be,G2.ce] (g0=TR1/Q3, g1=TR2/Q1, g2=TR3/Q2):
  dc_bias = [-2.426, +4.084, -4.105, +6.510, +5.365, +3.870]
TR1's Vbe DC source term (G0.be) is NEGATIVE −2.43V. The NR residual is F_i = known_a[i] − v_i − R_i·i_i(v) + ΣS[i][j]·b_j (solver.rs:962). A negative known_a on TR1's be-port drives Vbe toward cutoff. Runtime ring confirms: s1/g0 settles Vbe=+0.36V, Vce=+21.7V (rail — TR1 in cutoff), Ic≈7µA, gm≈2.8e-4 (~120x below design 0.033). Meanwhile g1(TR2) Vbe=0.66 gm=0.13, g2(TR3) Vbe=0.59 — output Darlington correctly biased. Static diag linearization already shows G0:be v_op=0.4959 gm=4.19e-4 (wrong) vs G1/G2 0.6446 gm=4.35e-3. Realized stage gain ~0.46x (−6.7dB) → the −49.5dB deficit.

WHY ONLY TR1. TR1's base bias is the ONLY one that does NOT come from a VCC divider: it is set by R2 (Rfb 56k) FROM THE FEEDBACK BUS (nfb), whose DC level is established by the conducting output Darlington via the DC-coupled NFB (out→R7→RV1→bus). The linear-superposition vcc_injection cannot reproduce a servo whose set-point depends on the nonlinear devices being ON, so it lands TR1's be-source at −2.43V. TR2/TR3 sit on direct VCC/collector paths the linear solve does capture.

THE vbe CLAMP DOESN'T SAVE IT. compute_dc_bias has a guard (general.rs:919): if dc_bias[be].abs() < 0.65 → force ±0.65. |−2.43|>0.65 so the clamp NO-OPs for TR1; the bad −2.43V passes through. (The clamp only rescues ports the linear solve left near zero.)

CONFIRMED NOT the suspects from 685e: convergence healthy (≤2 NR iters after settle), transconductance exact, scattering S is correct passive scattering, input port not the loss. It is purely the DC operating-point SOURCE term feeding the NR.

RELATION TO ko5g (g725). This IS the ko5g thesis made concrete: the runtime DC-bias injection is a fragmented LINEAR approximation (vcc_injection→dc_bias) that diverges from the validated NONLINEAR DC solve. The static bias (optrace/compute_dc_voltages → the 0.94/0.30 = Vbe 0.64 validation) is computed by a full nonlinear Newton DC solve but is NEVER injected into the runtime stage's dc_bias. The triode path ALREADY solved exactly this (general.rs:269-284, 1542-1582: compute_triode_dc_qpoint + apply_triode_dc_qpoint OVERRIDES stage.dc_bias[0]=dc.vgk with the nonlinear-solved value). There is NO BJT analogue. The fix = g725.2's prize: feed bias.rs BiasSeed (nonlinear DC node voltages) into the BJT be/ce dc_bias terms so TR1's base servo set-point (0.94V → Vbe 0.64) is HELD, not the linear −2.43V.

PROPOSED FIX (deferred — entangled with ko5g, per Rule 1). Add a BJT DC Q-point seed mirroring apply_triode_dc_qpoint: after assemble, take the nonlinear DC node voltages (bias.rs BiasSeed / compute_dc_voltages incl. the BJT Shockley servo), compute each BJT's Vbe/Vce at the true Q-point, and OVERRIDE dc_bias[be]/dc_bias[ce] (and warm-start v_prev) for the grouped BJT path — replacing the linear vcc_injection terms for be/ce ports. Surgical insertion point: general.rs after line 284 (a compute_bjt_dc_qpoint/apply_bjt_dc_qpoint pair). NOT applied here: it requires wiring the nonlinear BiasSeed into the runtime stage, which is precisely the ko5g.2 migration (risky, owns the bias core) — forcing a one-off seed here would duplicate/pre-empt that machinery. Recommend landing as ko5g.2 (g725.2) with the BA283 golden as the acceptance gate.

CLI: pedalkernel diag pedals/500/1073/sub/ba283.pedal --ipc /tmp/ba283.pkdiag --tail --tail-amp 0.1 --tail-freq 1000 --tail-blocks 40 --knob Gain=0.5

=== BA283 NR REPORT (PRIMARY DELIVERABLE) ===
Drove BA283 @ 1kHz/0.1V, Gain=0.5, 48 blocks of 128 samples after warmup.
- CONVERGENCE: healthy every block — max_iters=2, max_residual=2.2e-5, 256 solves/block. (Block 0 = DC ramp: 131k solves while bias ramps in; settles by block 2.)
- TRANSCONDUCTANCE IS APPLIED: dIc/(gm·dVbe) measured 0.995 (TR1), 1.031 (Darlington TR2/TR3), 1.007 (g2) across the signal swing — ratio≈1, so Ic tracks gm·dVbe exactly at every operating point. The solve applies the BJT transconductance correctly.
- BUT the input transistor TR1 (group 0) is STARVED NEAR CUTOFF at runtime: Vbe≈0.36V (a conducting Si BJT needs ~0.65V), Ic≈7µA, realized gm≈2.7e-4 S — ~120× BELOW the design 0.033 S. Its gm exactly equals Ic/Vt for that starved Ic, so the device model is self-consistent; the operating point is wrong. (The Darlington g1 is correctly biased: Vbe≈0.662, Ic≈2.5mA, gm≈0.137.)
- REALIZED GAIN over the window: 0.32–0.61x (peak ~0.61x = -4.3 dB) vs design ~97x (+39.8 dB).
- The static snapshot's cross_gm shows the DESIGNED 0.033 (G0:ce=0.0399) because it's evaluated at the seeded warm-start bias; the live NR drives TR1 off. This is exactly what Phase B was built to reveal and the static S could not.

READ/VERDICT: The -49.5 dB is NOT a transconductance-application bug (dIc≈gm·dVbe holds). It is a DC OPERATING-POINT bug — the input BJT TR1 settles ~near cutoff (Vbe 0.36V vs the DC-validated ~0.64V) at runtime, so its realized gm is ~120x too low and the input stage delivers almost no gain. The fix belongs in the BA283 DC bias / NR steady-state for TR1 (the R2 56k base bias path / dc_bias injection establishing TR1's operating point), NOT in the scattering or the transconductance math. Next: audit why the grouped-NR settles TR1's base to 0.36V despite the validated DC bias (suspect: the dc_bias/VCC Norton injection for the input port vs the feedback-bus bias path).

comments.text:
DELIVERED — BA283 MNA snapshot captured + IPC file working. Commits 568e711c (rt accessors) + ae2459df (std IPC+CLI) on branch 9u6u.1-mna-diag-ipc.

BUILD/TEST: cargo build -p pedalkernel (default, diag OFF) GREEN; --features diag GREEN; clippy clean. Tests: diag_ipc roundtrip ok; subcircuit_expand 13/13 ok; neve1073_spice ba283 3/3 ok. Disk hit ENOSPC mid-session (105Mi) — reclaimed by removing this worktree's target/debug/incremental (NOT cargo clean), recovered to 11Gi; no goldens/source touched.

CLI: 'pedalkernel diag <pedal> [--ipc <out>] [--knob K=V]' compiles+captures+(writes)+prints; 'pedalkernel diag --ipc <file>' mmaps+prints. IPC format v1: magic PKDIAG\0\1 + 32B LE binary header (version, section_count, mna_kind=JSON, mna_offset=32, mna_len, reserved=PhaseB hook) + JSON DiagSnapshot body. memmap2 on std host; rt side stays no_std (DiagSnapshot/MnaStageSnapshot are plain Vec/String + gated serde).

BA283 (Gain=0.5): compiles to 3 stages [Wdf, MultiNl, Wdf]. The MultiNl stage = 6 NL ports (3 NPN BjtNpn2P, each be+ce) + 3 reactive caps + 1 adapted parent => 10x10 S. Input via ADAPTED WDF port (R=1000ohm, the hardcoded input-Z from engine-adapted-input-port memory); output via extract_coeffs (extract_vs=0); vs_injection=None.

SMOKING GUNS for the -49.5dB/0.324x collapse:
1. Adapted INPUT port is NOT adapted: S[9][9]=-0.387 (should be ~0). The input parent port reflects ~39% of incident — the R-type adaptor's parent port is mismatched.
2. S[9][3]=S[adapted][G1.ce]=-1.016, |S|>1 — input over-couples to Q1 collector. A passive R-adaptor S should be bounded; >1 entry signals the scattering derivation is off for this port set.
3. Port-R != 1/gm by orders of magnitude. Textbook gm=dIc/dVbe (cross_gm): Q1/Q2 ce = 3.26e-2 S -> 1/gm~30.7ohm, but those CE ports carry Rp=604/2963ohm and the BE ports are adapted off the DIAGONAL self-conductance (dIb/dVbe=4.35e-3 -> 230ohm), NOT the transconductance. The companion linearization adapts each port to its self-conductance, so the gm-driven current gain (beta*) never enters the port impedance -> the CE port sees a huge Rp and the stage delivers ~unity instead of ~97x.
   Per-device (Gain=0.5): Q3(TR1 input CE): v_op4.50 gm_self1.08e-5 cross_gm3.99e-2; Q1(TR2): cross_gm3.26e-2; Q2(TR3 2N3055): cross_gm3.26e-2. be ports v_op 0.496/0.645/0.645.

INTERP: realized open-loop A collapses because the BJT transconductance (cross_gm ~ 0.033 S, the actual gain mechanism) is NOT reflected into the adapted CE port resistance — the port is adapted to the tiny SELF conductance instead, and the input parent port is mis-adapted (S[9][9]!=0, |S[9][3]|>1). Hand-computing A/beta from this S confirms the gain mechanism is dropped at the WDF port-adaptation boundary, consistent with bead pedalkernel-685e (boundary-scaling vs in-matrix deficit -> this is an IN-MATRIX/port-adaptation deficit). Full-precision S/gm in the IPC JSON.

DEFERRED to Phase B (9u6u.2): live runtime ring (SolverStats + per-stage levels + evolving scattering) appended after the JSON section via the reserved header field; lock-free MetricsRingBuffer over the mmap region; CLI live-tail.

TRADEOFF (Rule 1): chose JSON for the static MNA section (self-describing, diffable, simpler than binary for one-shot capture) but kept a BINARY versioned header so Phase B's lock-free ring is a fixed binary layout after the JSON body. diag is its own cargo feature OFF by default (serde+serde_json+memmap2) so the default dep graph/build is unchanged.

title: BA283 -49.5dB: measure realized gain + localize (boundary-scaling vs in-matrix deficit)
description: BA283 compiles to ONE MultiNl co-solving 3 BJTs, NFB fused in the 6x6 scattering (confirmed via debug --json, PR #173). Shape-exact, level -49.5dB. Single-sine golden can't split: (a) loop co-solved right but signal scaled at input/output boundary (hardcoded 1000ohm input port) = pure level, vs (b) MultiNl realizes ~300x too little gain = in-matrix deficit. Measure per-stage signal levels through the chain (in -> Wdf Cin -> MultiNl -> Wdf Cout -> out) to LOCALIZE the 300x loss + report the verdict. The discriminator for where the gain fix goes.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
MEASUREMENT COMPLETE (branch 685e-ba283-gain-measure, pushed). Env-gated probe BA283_LEVELS=1 instruments CompiledPedal::process(); test ba283_stage_levels drives the BA283 with the golden 1kHz/0.1V sine (Gain=0.5, warmup n/2, 19200-sample settled window).

PER-STAGE LEVEL TABLE (peak-abs / RMS):
  input            peak=1.000e-1  rms=7.071e-2
  stage0 (Wdf Cin) peak=1.000e-1  rms=7.071e-2   in->out = +0.00 dB  (unity)
  stage1 (MultiNl) peak=3.243e-2  rms=2.294e-2   in->out = -9.78 dB  (gain 0.324x)
  stage2 (Wdf Cout)peak=3.354e-2  rms=2.294e-2   in->out = +0.00 dB  (unity)
  output           peak=3.350e-2  rms=2.294e-2
  realized chain gain (out/in) = 0.3244x  (-9.78 dB)
  golden chain gain            = 97.29x   (+39.76 dB)
  WDF-vs-golden gap            = -49.54 dB  (matches the established -49.5 dB)

VERDICT: hypothesis (b) IN-MATRIX DEFICIT. The loss is localized ENTIRELY to the MultiNl.
- NOT boundary scaling (a): in->stage0 is exactly unity (+0.00 dB); the input port does NOT attenuate the signal ~300x. The hardcoded ~1000ohm input-port impedance is NOT where the level is lost.
- NOT output coupling: stage1->stage2->output are exactly unity (+0.00 dB).
- The MultiNl's OWN in->out gain is 0.324x (-9.78 dB, an ATTENUATION) where the designed BA283 closed-loop gain must be ~97x (+39.76 dB) -- since both bracketing coupling stages are unity, the MultiNl alone must deliver the full +39.76 dB. The MultiNl realizes 97.29/0.324 = ~300x too little gain. The 6x6 co-solve (NFB fused) produces a closed-loop gain ~300x below design despite the validated DC bias.

=> The gain fix belongs INSIDE the MultiNl co-solve (injection/scattering/model), NOT at the input-port impedance boundary. Next step: audit the MultiNl's NL-root injection + the s_nl_adapted scattering vs the designed open-loop/closed-loop gain (Norton source-term / port-vs-device-current convention is the prime suspect, per the WDF NR solver memo).

Instrumentation committed (env-gated, off by default, reusable; probe-off output byte-identical -- 0.0229 V, -49.5 dB). tb303 excluded; golden is ngspice-derived (not bootstrapped). Bead left in_progress; no PR opened.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: S-AUDIT (full 10x10 via diag tool, PR #175): static S is the PASSIVE scattering (small BJT self-reflections ~0.02-0.05, be<->ce coupling ~symmetric). cross_gm (0.033, transconductance) IS captured in the linearization and belongs in the per-sample NR Jacobian, NOT the port-R. => the agent's 'cross_gm not in port impedance' anomaly is RETRACTED. Confirmed minor: input port S[9][9]=-0.387 (~2-4dB). The -49.5dB gain deficit is in the DYNAMIC per-sample NR (applying the BJT transconductance against S), which the static snapshot can't show. Next: Phase B runtime ring to watch the NR.

comments.text: ROOT CAUSE (Phase B runtime ring, MEASURED): DC operating-point bug. Live NR: convergence healthy, transconductance EXACT (dIc/(gm*dVbe)=0.995-1.031). Input TR1 settles near cutoff at runtime Vbe=0.36V (validated ~0.64V), Ic=7uA, gm=2.7e-4 (~120x below design 0.033) -> input stage ~no gain -> -49.5dB. Output Darlington correctly biased. === BA283 ANSWER (the unblocker) ===
File: pedalkernel-pro/pedals/500/1073/sub/ba283.pedal (self-contained, no use(...)).
ONE MultiNl stage co-solving ALL THREE BJTs — NOT three NlWdf stages.

  id 0  Wdf      "Cin"                                    flow=0    nl_root=0 nl_port=0 fb=0
  id 1  MultiNl  "Ccmp,Cfb,Cmil,Q1,Q2,Q3,R3,R4,R6,R7,RU1,Rcmp,Rfb,Rin"  flow=82  nl_root=3 nl_port=6 fb=0
  id 2  Wdf      "Cout,RL"                                flow=128  nl_root=0 nl_port=0 fb=0

Prose dump confirms: MultiNlStage(n_nl=6, n_passive=3, solver=GROUPED) with 3 groups: BjtNpn2P, BjtNpn2P, BjtNpn2P (TR1/TR2/TR3, each a 2-port -> 6 NL ports). feedback_ports=0: the DC-coupled shunt NFB (output->R7->RV1->bus->R2->TR1 base) is FUSED into the single 6x6 scattering matrix — there is NO runtime feedback port. So a "gain fix" cannot target a feedback port; it must act through the co-solved MNA/scattering of the one MultiNl stage (bias, device models, the in-matrix NFB resistors).

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
IMPL START (g725.2-bjt-dc-qpoint, off 9u6u.2-runtime-ring + #163 bias.rs(pr/163) + main; build green w/ diag).

BASELINE diag ring (pedalkernel diag ba283.pedal --tail --knob Gain=0.5 --tail-freq 1000 --tail-amp 0.1), settled:
  g0=TR1 Vbe=+0.362 Vce=+21.69(rail/cutoff) Ic=7.1uA gm=0.00028  <-- broken (~120x low)
  g1=TR2 Vbe=+0.662 gm=0.137  (correct)
  g2=TR3 Vbe=+0.590 gm=0.0021
  chain gain=0.328x (-9.67 dB)  -> matches the -49.5 dB golden gap.

UNIFIED-PATH ASSESSMENT (Rule 1): bias.rs BjtNpnSeed::locate_bias_topology REQUIRES a classic base divider R1(base->vcc)+R2(base->gnd). BA283 TR1 has NEITHER: base is fed ONLY by Rfb 56k from the DC-coupled NFB bus (nfb), whose DC level is set by the conducting Darlington (TR2/TR3). The seed solves ONE device against a linear NetworkBias divider; it cannot co-solve a 3-BJT feedback servo, and would error UndeterminableBjt{BaseDivider} on TR1. Both linear DC solvers in-tree (bias_analysis::compute_dc_voltages AND bias.rs::solve_network_bias) are resistor-only MNA -> same failure mode as the broken compute_dc_bias vcc-injection. The validated 0.94/0.30 (Vbe 0.64) comes from an EXTERNAL nonlinear schematic-trace, not a runtime path.
=> Wiring BjtNpnSeed into the runtime stage does NOT fix BA283 (it's structurally a per-device divider solver). Taking the bead-authorized LOCAL fallback: a compute_bjt_dc_qpoint that does a proper NONLINEAR nodal DC solve co-solving ALL grouped BJTs (Gummel-Poon junctions + group resistors, rails fixed) -> reads Vbe/Vce per device -> apply_bjt_dc_qpoint overrides dc_bias[be]/[ce] + warm-start v_prev (mirrors apply_triode_dc_qpoint at general.rs:282-284). Model sourced from the SAME helpers::gummel_poon_model the runtime uses. Unification remainder (extend BiasSeed to a co-solved-servo topology) banked to g725 epic.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED + GATED (branch g725.2-bjt-dc-qpoint, pushed; commit e74283a8; NO PR per instruction). Bead stays in_progress.

WHAT LANDED (rigid/general.rs + pedalkernel-rt/stage.rs):
- compute_bjt_dc_qpoint: full-network NONLINEAR nodal Newton DC solve over a grouped-BJT stage (Gummel-Poon junctions co-solved against the group resistors, rails fixed, gmin=1e-9 regularization, 0.25V/iter voltage-limiting, residual-converged). Took the bead-authorized LOCAL fallback, NOT bias.rs BjtNpnSeed — that seed REQUIRES a classic R1(base->vcc)+R2(base->gnd) divider and would error UndeterminableBjt on BA283 TR1 (base fed ONLY by Rfb 56k from the NFB bus). The unified BiasSeed is structurally a per-device divider solver; co-solving the 3-BJT feedback servo is the unification remainder (banked to g725).
- apply_bjt_dc_qpoint + MultiNlStage::apply_dc_qpoint_seed: map solved node voltages -> per-port v*, warm-start v_prev, and derive dc_bias by EXACT inversion of the runtime NR residual dc_bias[i]=v_i+R_i*i_i - Σ_j S[i][j]*(v_j-R_j*i_j) - Σ_k s_passive[i][k]*b_passive[k]. New stage fields dc_qpoint_v/dc_qpoint_passive_b; re-applied after recompute_scattering (pot moves re-extract linear dc_bias) and on reset(). Caps pre-charged via wdf_set_incident(b_passive) so the first sample sees the right reflected wave.

VERIFIED CORRECT (diag runtime ring, PK_BJT_DCQPOINT=1):
- DC solve: BA283 TR1 -> base=0.996V, Vbe=0.608V (matches validated 0.94 / 0.64). TR2 Vbe=0.54, TR3(2N3055) Vbe=0.40.
- Inversion: v* is an EXACT fixed point of the runtime NR — self-check max|F(v*)| ≈ 9e-16.
- nl_kinds order is [TR3,TR2,TR1] (reverse of the trace's assumed g0=TR1; diag g0=TR3 ports[0,1], g2=TR1 ports[4,5]) — handled by node-identity mapping, not order.

WHY IT IS GATED OFF (PK_BJT_DCQPOINT, default off): seeding makes the grouped NR + REACTIVE ports a JOINT equilibrium the static seed does not stabilize. v* holds for ~2 samples, then the DC-coupled NFB caps drift off b_passive (the cap incident wave from scatter_all at v* != b_passive), the grouped NR stops converging (residual ~27, budget-exhausted) and BA283 goes unstable. The cap-feedback DC equilibrium is the banked deep-WDF fix (engine-adapted-input-port / cosolve family), NOT this bead's surface (Rule 1).

ACCEPTANCE GATES:
1. BA283 golden: does NOT fully close in this bead. OFF (default) = baseline -49.5 dB (WDF RMS 0.0229V) byte-identical. ON (opt-in) = -31.4 dB (WDF RMS 0.1857V, ~8x louder, +18 dB recovered) but unstable. Full closure is blocked on the joint NL+reactive DC-equilibrium stabilization.
2. NO REGRESSION (proven): default code path is byte-identical (gate off => compute/apply never called; new fields default None/empty => apply_dc_qpoint_seed is a no-op). Lib suite: branch 181 fails == base(3d4c21aa) 181 fails, IDENTICAL SET (comm -23/-13 both empty: zero new, zero flips). The 181 are pre-existing on the 9u6u.2+#163+main base (goldenrod/ratking/screamer/pultec WIP). Goldens: legends_spice 16/16 (fuzz/muff/blues/screamer/rat/klon), drums 6/6, dual_golden 6/6, tape_head, compressor 1/1, neve1073_spice 4/4 all PASS. rt-lib 2 fails (IIR + StateSpace processor tests) + validate pultec rlc_makeup_gain — all pre-existing, untouched by the diff (touches only the BJT-DC path).

RELATION TO ko5g: g725.2 is NOT complete. Delivered: the missing BJT DC-qpoint pass (analogue of the triode pair) + verified nonlinear DC solve + exact wave-domain dc_bias inversion + survives-recompute machinery + precise RCA. Remainder to close BA283: (a) stabilize v* as a JOINT NL-port + reactive-port DC equilibrium (deep WDF, banked) and/or (b) the unified-BiasSeed servo-topology extension. Recommend a follow-up child for the stabilization.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
TRACE (read-only, signal_flow.rs):

PIPELINE: find_active_elements(:93, port-semantic, GENERIC) -> build_flow_graph(:327, directed edges) -> tarjan_scc(:481, cycles=feedback) -> feedback_edges(:1909). feedback_ports=0 => no multi-element SCC formed.

ROOT CAUSE (A) — detection, build_flow_graph:
- active_output_blocks_passive_reachability(:198) returns TRUE (block) for EVERY active output node; only exception is shunt diodes (:205 is_diode_family && on-rail). So when BFS-ing element i's output to find feedback back-edges, ALL other active outputs are blocked (:362-376).
- Also blocks graph.in_node + graph.out_node (:377-378) and uses restricted-reachability for barrier inputs (:399-460, feedback_input_is_barrier).
- These heuristics are OP-AMP-CASCADE-TUNED: comments at :323-360 cite U1/U2, Klon, Screamer, Fuzz Face. They kill FALSE backward edges in op-amp chains (clean isolated stage outputs).
- BA283 = Darlington TR1+TR2 + 3rd CE stage TR3 + a SHARED global feedback bus (out->R7->RV1->bus; TR2-E->R6->bus; R2 56k bus->TR3 base). The bus shares nodes with transistor outputs -> blanket block-all-active-outputs CUTS the feedback path -> back-edge TR2->TR3 never forms -> no SCC -> feedback_ports=0 -> Cascade -> -49.5 dB.

title: Retire build_opamp_nl_feedback: route op-amp+NL feedback through build_general_mna co-solve
description: build_opamp_nl_feedback is a redundant, strictly-inferior shortcut. It applies the op-amp closed-loop gain forward (compute_vs_voltage) then clips the diode separately, so the diode solves against the op-amp OUTPUT impedance, not the closed-loop impedance (wrong Thevenin) — the ~1.6-2x over-hot TS/SD-1 error. Retire it; route vcvs+nl groups to build_general_mna, which stamps the op-amp VCVS and grouped-NR co-solves the diode against it. HARD: do NOT revert on golden miss — keep for diagnostics, escalate.

title: Root-cause vari-mu 6386 harmonic gap (spectral 112dB) — bias/operating-point vs model-coeff
description: EL34 pentode harmonic gap was a VBIAS(fixed)-vs-auto-bias(Rk) operating-point mismatch deck-vs-engine. Vari-mu 6386: spectral 112.4dB / THD 11dB (amplitude RMS/peak perfect 0.0dB -> harmonic structure wrong). PRELIM: 6386 is NOT the same bias-source issue (both deck varimu_6386.spice + circuits/active/varimu_6386.pedal use Rk=1ohm + Ck=1000u auto-bias, 1M grid leak). BUT: (a) deck .IC V(v_plate)=132 vs .pedal supply 300V -> operating-point mismatch on the remote-cutoff curve; (b) deck behavioral curve (3.981e-8*PWR(Vak,2.383)/PWR(0.5-0.1*Vgk,1.8)) coefficients vs engine vari_mu.rs ge_6386 params. Investigate which drives the 112dB harmonic divergence: operating-point (plate V / Vgk) or model-form/coeff mismatch. Read-only: compare deck model+OP vs vari_mu.rs ge_6386; small ngspice OP/bias-sensitivity check ok.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
VERDICT: (c)-adjacent but NOT the EL34 bias-source class — root cause is a TRANSIENT/OPERATING-POINT capture failure on BOTH sides, masking + amplified by an engine-side missing VariMu DC-bias seed. Model coefficients are byte-identical (vari_mu.rs:60-69 == spice deck Bip lines 130-134), and the DC target operating point matches (Vb=300V/Rp=10k/Vgk=-2V -> Vak=132V/Ia=16.8mA on BOTH sides; deck '.IC v_plate=132' is that same Q-point, NOT a different supply — preliminary 132V-vs-300V read was a misread). So (a) literal VBIAS-mismatch = ruled out, (b) coefficient-mismatch = ruled out.

THE REAL FINDING (FFT of golden/tubes/varimu_6386/{sine.npy,wdf/sine.npy}, fs=48k, 400ms): NEITHER golden contains the intended 1kHz tone as a fundamental. ngspice golden = pure DC-settling transient: monotonic plate decay 108V->13V, energy at DC/2.5Hz/5Hz, mean still drifting (15V) in the last 100ms, ZERO 1kHz fundamental, 0 upward zero-crossings over 400ms. Engine golden = starts cold at exactly 0.0 for 30+ samples then rings at ~125Hz (120/130Hz sidebands), also no 1kHz fundamental. corr(ng_ac, en_ac) ~= -0.01 (uncorrelated), opposite asymmetry (ng pos/|neg|=2.07, en=0.78). The reported 112.4dB spectral / 11.0dB THD 'divergence' is therefore an artifact of comparing two differently-broken transient captures, not a steady-state harmonic comparison.

TWO INDEPENDENT BUGS:
1) SPICE deck never reaches steady state in the 400ms window. Cathode bypass Ck=1000uF + supply filter_cap=1000uF w/ 50ohm source => tau~50ms, ~250ms+ to settle; '.IC v_plate=132' only seeds the plate, not the caps, so ngspice .tran runs the full RC charge and the 1kHz AC is swamped. ngspice does .op before .tran so it 'should' start settled — the cap IC=0 on Ck and the supply RC defeat that here.
2) ENGINE never seeds VariMu DC bias. spqr_build.rs:2755 set_bias() block has a RootKind::Triode(Koren) arm and a RootKind::Bjt arm but NO RootKind::VariMu arm — vari-mu keeps default vgk_bias=-2.0 (vari_mu.rs:127) and starts from cold cap state (output=0 for first samples), then the cathode/supply RC + drive produce the 125Hz artifact rather than a settled 1kHz tone. Even where Vgk=-2 happens to be the right DC value, the cold-start cap transient + no Q-point warm-start (unlike the Koren/BJT paths which seed cap + initial_prev_v) means the engine never reaches the 1kHz steady state inside the window either.

RECOMMENDED FIX TARGET (in priority order): (i) FIX THE GOLDENS/HARNESS FIRST — extend capture window or settle-then-measure (drop the transient, e.g. ngspice .tran with UIC off + longer prerun, and engine warm-start) so both sides actually present a 1kHz steady-state tone before the metric runs; the current 112dB number is not a valid harmonic measurement. (ii) ENGINE: add a RootKind::VariMu(t) arm to the spqr_build.rs:2755 set_bias block mirroring the Triode/BJT seeding (set_bias(dc.vgk) + cathode-cap seed + initial_prev_v warm-start) so vari-mu reaches its Q-point immediately like the other tube/transistor paths. (iii) Re-measure after (i)+(ii); only then judge any residual genuine harmonic gap. This is an OPERATING-POINT/transient-settling class issue (spiritually akin to EL34) but the mechanism is missing-bias-seed + unsettled-caps, NOT a fixed-VBIAS-vs-autobias source mismatch. RECOMMENDED_AGENT: rust-supervisor for (ii); harness/golden owner for (i). Evidence files: pedalkernel-rt/src/elements/nonlinear/vari_mu.rs:60-69,127; pedalkernel/src/compiler/spqr_build.rs:2755-2758; pedalkernel-rt/src/stage.rs:1045-1046; spice-circuits/active/varimu_6386.spice:80,93-94,153; circuits/active/varimu_6386.pedal:13-16,29-30.

comments.text: Completed: deck now converges with push-pull signature. Three root causes: (1) TRANSFORMER WINDING POLARITY: Lp2 reversed vct->vp2_m so K_s2 coupling ADDS to K_s1 in Ls instead of cancelling. Before: H2=5373% THD, fundamental zero. After: H2=3.3ppm (-110dB), H3 dominant (77.5ppm). (2) KOREN ATAN MODEL: replaced TANH(Vak/15) with (base^EX/KG1)*atan(Vpk/KVB) using pentodes.model params MU=8.7 EX=1.35 KG1=1460 KP=48 KVB=12. (3) STIFF-DECK: 100k-500kOhm parallel damping on all inductors breaks stiff L-mesh that caused 'timestep too small' under harness RELTOL=1e-6 (harness overrides our RELTOL but not DELMAX=57e-6). Also added Einv E-source for V2 differential drive. Verified harness-equiv run: 19547 rows no errors, H1=585mV H2=1.96uV H3=45.4uV THD=0.0078%. PR: https://github.com/ajmwagar/pedalkernel/pull/140. LEARNED: In a center-tapped PP OT SPICE model, Lp2 must have reversed terminal order vs Lp1. Both plates connect to the same CT node; with same-direction L definitions both K_sN couplings to Ls cancel. Reversed Lp2 makes them add. LEARNED: ngspice rejects K<0 (explodes numerically); fix winding polarity by reversing the L element terminals instead.

title: Root-cause MOSFET THD/spectral gap (nmos_common_source SPEC 202, pmos_source_follower SPEC 138)
description: Real nonlinear gap (NOT metric artifact: high spectral, not just THD). MOSFETs distinct from JFETs (NonlinearKind::Mosfet). nmos_common_source: spectral 201.6dB, THD 137; pmos_source_follower: spectral 138, THD 149. Root-cause the MOSFET device model / WDF root vs ngspice. Read-only: compare committed WDF .npy vs ngspice golden spectra (numpy), read the Mosfet model + solver path. NO JFET/OTA/BJT (handled separately).

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (READ-ONLY investigation, no build needed — golden-vs-golden numpy + source trace).

SPECTRAL SIGNATURE (FFT of committed goldens, f0=125Hz):
- nmos_common_source: ngspice DC=+1.19V, swing -2.87..+7.37, h1=2.28e4, h2=2.8e3 (~12% H2, strong even-order = real square-law distortion). WDF: DC=+0.0003V, swing +-0.10, h1=960, h2=0.065 (THD ~0.007%). WDF is a PURE LINEAR PASSTHROUGH at ~input level, no bias, no harmonics.
- pmos_source_follower: ngspice DC=+5.17V (biased), h2=197. WDF: DC=+0.0006V, swing +-0.50, h2=0.0096 (THD ~0.0002%). Same signature: linear passthrough, unbiased.
=> Both failures have the SAME root cause: the MOSFET never conducts and never distorts.

ROOT CAUSE (model FORM/integration bug, not a deck-vs-engine parameter mismatch):
The MOSFET's gate-source voltage Vgs is NEVER driven by the input signal in the audio path.
- pedalkernel-rt/src/stage.rs:1035-1064 set_control_voltage() has match arms for Triode/VariMu/Bjt/DiffPair/Pentode but NO RootKind::Mosfet arm -> falls through to '_ => {}' no-op (line 1062). So the up-front control set at stage.rs:2076 does nothing for MOSFETs.
- The only writer of Mosfet Vgs is set_mosfet_vgs() (stage.rs:3055), called ONLY from ModulationTarget::MosfetVgs (processor.rs:3129,3363) i.e. LFO/envelope modulation — never from the signal path.
- create_root() builds RootKind::Mosfet(MosfetRoot::new(model)) (build.rs:166); MosfetRoot::new sets vgs=0.0 (mosfet.rs:177). The multi-NL host path (build.rs:76-89) explicitly documents this: 'Vgs only changes via explicit modulation (floating gate => 0 V, channel off)'.
- With vgs=0: overdrive() (mosfet.rs:136-148) returns None for NMOS (0<=Vth=2.1) and PMOS (0>=Vth) => ids()=0 always (mosfet.rs:90-93). Device is permanently in CUTOFF. The residual WDF output is just the passive R-network passing input through with the MOSFET as an open/leakage element => linear, ~0 DC, ~0 THD. Exactly matches the measured signature.

WHY ngspice differs: ngspice solves the full DC operating point — the R1/R2 (NMOS) / RG (PMOS) gate bias network sets Vgs above/below Vth so the device conducts, the signal modulates Vgs through C1, and square-law gives gain + even harmonics. The engine has no equivalent: no gate-bias-network analysis and no signal->Vgs path for MOSFETs.

PROPOSED FIX (rust-supervisor):
1. PRIMARY: drive MOSFET Vgs from the signal path. Add a RootKind::Mosfet arm in set_control_voltage() (stage.rs:1041) mirroring the BJT/Triode pattern: m.set_vgs(vgs_bias + input*compensation), AND establish a vgs_bias (DC operating point from the gate-bias network) at compile/build time — analogous to BJT set_bias()/vbe_bias() and Triode vgk_bias(). Without the DC bias term the device still won't conduct (input AC alone won't cross Vth). This requires the compiler to compute the gate DC voltage from the R-divider (NMOS: Vg=VDD*R2/(R1+R2)=9*47/147=2.88V => Vgs=Vg-Vsource) and pass it through, the same way BJT/triode bias is derived.
2. SECONDARY (only matters once it conducts; still wrong): (a) square-law factor of 2 — SPICE LEVEL=1 uses Id=(Kp/2)(W/L)(Vgs-Vth)^2(1+lambda*Vds), but mosfet.rs:100,103 use kp*... with NO /2 (2x current). (b) PMOS params wrong vs deck: p_bs250() (mosfet.rs:60-66) has vth=-1.5/kp=0.07/lambda=0.04 but pmos_source_follower.spice has VTO=-3.5/KP=0.05/LAMBDA=0.03. (c) Triode region also missing the /2 (mosfet.rs:100 vs SPICE Id=(Kp/2)(2*Vov*Vds - Vds^2)). NMOS deck params (VTO=2.1,KP=0.1,LAMBDA=0.04) match n_2n7000() except the /2.

Note: nmos and pmos share the SAME primary root cause (no signal->Vgs + no DC bias). They DIFFER only in secondary parameter accuracy (PMOS model constants are also wrong vs its deck; NMOS constants match apart from the /2). Status left in_progress.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: OWNER: MOSFET common-source Q-point fix is already in flight elsewhere. NOT dispatching a duplicate. Root cause captured: no RootKind::Mosfet arm in set_control_voltage (stage.rs:1035-1064) + no DC gate-bias derived from divider -> permanent cutoff/linear passthrough. SECONDARY to fold into that fix: square-law missing /2 (mosfet.rs:100,103; SPICE LEVEL=1 uses Kp/2), and PMOS p_bs250 constants wrong vs deck (vth -1.5 vs deck -3.5, kp .07 vs .05, lambda .04 vs .03).

title: Root-cause diode-clipper spectral gap (single_diode SPEC 218/161, opamp_diode_clipper SPEC 215/209)
description: Real nonlinear harmonic gap: high SPECTRAL (218/215dB) even where THD-ratio is low. single_diode + opamp_diode_clipper. Diode IV / clipping harmonic structure diverges from ngspice. Read-only: compare committed WDF vs ngspice .npy spectra (numpy), read the diode model + WDF root NR / K-table path. Note: diode is the canonical nonlinear case; this likely also explains TS808/RAT/bigmuff clipping character.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (two distinct, neither is a diode-NL/KTable harmonic bug):

== single_diode (mild 223.7dB / hard 178.1dB) = SPECTRAL-METRIC EDGE CASE, NOT engine bug ==
Signature: BROADBAND across ~24-45 inter-harmonic bins, ALL at the noise floor. The worst bin (9850Hz, bin1970) is NOT a 1kHz harmonic; ref=-92.8dB, wdf=-316.5dB. WDF is numerically pristine (median bin -314dB) while ngspice golden has broadband numerical 'grass' at -75 to -116dB (mild: 121/137 above-threshold bins are non-harmonic floor @ mean -95.5dB; hard: 132/165 @ mean -74dB). The real 1kHz harmonics h1..h8 AGREE within ~2dB; THD ratios match (hard ref 9.13% vs wdf 9.58%; mild 12.3% vs 16.1%). The 80dB-below-peak threshold is too permissive when peak is low (mild peak only -36.7dB => thr -116.7dB pulls in ngspice trunc/ADC noise). VERDICT: metric sensitivity, WDF diode model is correct. metrics.rs:211 spectral_error_db threshold_db = ref_peak_db - 80.0; loop 215-222 compares wdf -316dB vs ref noise-floor -92dB => 224dB false error.

== opamp_diode_clipper (linear 218.3dB / clipping 211.5dB) = BROKEN ngspice GOLDEN + DC-offset mismatch ==
Signature: SINGLE/two-bin, all energy at bin1-2 (DC, 2.5Hz) from Blackman-leakage of a static DC level. ngspice golden = essentially pure +5.05V DC: linear mean=5.0476 std=0.0004 (0.4mV AC!), clipping mean=5.0475 std=0.0036. WDF = AC-centered: linear mean=0.0 std=0.350 (~0.5Vpk), clipping std=0.715. Circuit is gain -10 on 50mV => expect ~500mV pk AC; WDF produces exactly that, ngspice golden produces NO AC swing. The ngspice ideal-opamp deck (Eop v_opamp_out 0 v_bias v_neg 100000, spice-circuits/canonical/opamp_diode_clipper.spice:33) sits at the 4.5V bias rail and does not develop AC gain in the .tran (run_validation.py:197 measures v(v_out) ~= v_opamp_out). So 218dB = DC-leakage bin1 (ngspice +5V vs WDF 0V). Two problems: (1) the ngspice golden is non-physical/broken (no gain), (2) DC operating-point mismatch: ngspice keeps the +4.5V bias on output, WDF outputs AC-only (no DC bias propagated). After removing DC from both, ref AC peak collapses to -79dB (linear) confirming ngspice has ~no AC. VERDICT: ngspice golden invalid for opamp_diode_clipper; cannot validate WDF against it.

PROPOSED FIXES:
(A) METRIC (single_diode): tighten spectral_error_db significance gate. Floor the threshold at an absolute level (e.g. max(ref_peak-80, -100dB)) OR require BOTH wdf and ref above a noise floor before scoring, OR only score at harmonic bins of the fundamental. metrics.rs:211. This removes the false 178-224dB and likely the TS808/RAT/bigmuff 'clipping-character' false gaps (same broadband-floor artifact).
(B) ENGINE+GOLDEN (opamp_diode_clipper): regenerate the ngspice golden - the Eop ideal-opamp .tran is not producing gain (verify ngspice convergence / virtual-ground DC bias). Separately the WDF vs ngspice DC convention differs (WDF AC-only output vs ngspice +4.5V bias); align output DC handling or DC-block both before comparison. Until the ngspice golden is fixed it cannot validate WDF; WDF output (gain -10, ~0.5Vpk, clipping at +-0.75V) looks physically correct.

NOT a KTable/Shockley/oversample harmonic bug - diode I-V harmonic structure matches ngspice where ngspice is valid.

comments.text:
# SPICE Validation Gate Audit — pedalkernel-ncjy

**Date:** 2026-06-15 | **Repository:** pedalkernel (main) | **Mode:** READ-ONLY

## Executive Summary

The SPICE validation gate contains **23 problematic metric checks** out of 53 total tests:
- **1 test:** NOT-GATED (silently unchecked)
- **10 tests:** THD disabled (≥150 dB threshold → never gates)
- **1 test:** Spectral disabled (279.4 dB, physically impossible)
- **11 tests:** POSITIVE RMS/PEAK thresholds (allow WDF to be WORSE than SPICE)

**Verdict:** The gate is configured to HIDE engine gaps, not measure them. Three categories of looseness exist:

1. **Disabled thresholds (honest admission of "not measuring")** — acceptable if documented
2. **Positive RMS/PEAK (calibrated-to-pass to allow failures)** — unacceptable, defeats test purpose
3. **Physically impossible spectral thresholds** — sign of placeholder, not real validation

---

## Detailed Findings by Suite

### 🔴 CRITICAL: NONLINEAR (5 tests, 4 disabled THD, 1 positive PEAK)

**Tests:** single_diode, diode_no_cap, diode_clipper, zener_clipper, common_cathode_12ax7

**Issue:** THD metrics are disabled (200 dB threshold) with comments saying "not meaningful at low levels"
but no measurement of what the actual error is.

**Risks:**
- A nonlinear circuit with 40 dB THD error passes (threshold 200 dB never gates)
- Example: Diode at low level with SPICE THD −40 dB, WDF THD 0 dB (40 dB error) → **PASS**
- No spectral gating on waveform shape differences

**Status:** ⚠️ NEEDS HONEST MEASUREMENT
- Either measure actual THD error (low/mid/high drive sweep) and set threshold
- Or set to None and admit it's ungated

**Current thresholds:**
| Test | RMS | PEAK | THD | SPEC |
|------|-----|------|-----|------|
| single_diode | -9.4 | -7.3 | **200** | — |
| diode_no_cap | -10.9 | -7.7 | **200** | — |
| diode_clipper | +5.1 | +8.0 | **200** | 173.4 |
| zener_clipper | -6.7 | +3.5 | **200** | — |
| common_cathode_12ax7 | +5.3 | +7.8 | **150** | 146.8 |

---

### 🔴 CRITICAL: ACTIVE DEVICES (10 tests, 3 positive, 1 with RMS +45, 1 spectral 279 dB)

**Tests:** jfet_source_follower, fuzz_face_pnp, push_pull_6l6, phase_allpass_stage, optical_attenuator, nmos_common_source, pmos_source_follower, npn_common_emitter, pnp_common_emitter, ota_ca3080

**Issue 1: Positive RMS/PEAK Thresholds (6 tests)**
- jfet_source_follower: RMS +1.0, PEAK +1.0 dB (marked "[LIMITED SUPPORT]")
- push_pull_6l6: RMS +45.0, PEAK +45.0 dB (fixture mismatch: DSL vs SPICE)
- Others with positive PEAK: optical_attenuator, nmos/pmos/npn/pnp gates, ota_ca3080

**Risk:** Positive thresholds allow WDF to be WORSE than SPICE and still pass.
- Example: if SPICE RMS = -10 dB and WDF RMS = +35 dB (45 dB worse), test PASSES push_pull_6l6 gate
- This inverts the purpose of the test: it becomes a "WDF-must-be-worse" gate

**Issue 2: Physically Impossible Spectral Threshold (phase_allpass_stage)**
- Spectral threshold: 279.4 dB
- This is far beyond the double-precision noise floor and cannot exist
- Comment: "Intentionally loose… sweep magnitude/phase match is excellent in time-domain"
- Means: the developer gave up on spectral gating and set an unattainable threshold

**Status:** ⚠️ NEEDS REDESIGN
- push_pull_6l6: Either align SPICE fixture to true pentode+transformer DSL, or mark pending
- phase_allpass_stage: Remove spectral threshold (set to None); rely on time-domain RMS/PEAK (1.0/1.0)
- jfet_source_follower: Mark as pending_reference (topology unsupported)
- Others (NMOS/PMOS/BJT/OTA): Thresholds are tight (0.7–1.7 dB); acceptable

---

### 🟡 WARNING: PEDALS (4 tests, 3 disabled THD, 1 with RMS +30, 1 peak +10)

**Tests:** ts808_clipper, rat_clipper, fuzz_core, bigmuff_stage

**Issue 1: Disabled THD (ts808, rat, fuzz_core)**
- TS808: THD 200 dB, comment: "Waveform shapes will differ"
- RAT: THD 200 dB
- Fuzz Core: THD 170 dB, comment: "Baseline: 163dB at very low levels"

**Issue 2: Inverted RMS/PEAK (bigmuff_stage)**
- RMS +30.0 dB, PEAK +10.0 dB (allow WDF 30dB worse than SPICE RMS)
- Comment: "Relaxed: waveform shapes will differ"
- No THD gate (disabled at 150 dB)

**Risk:** BigMuff allows WDF output to differ by 30 dB in RMS while claiming to test it.
- Example: SPICE RMS = -20 dB, WDF RMS = +10 dB → PASS (1000× worse)

**Status:** ⚠️ NEEDS HONEST MEASUREMENT
- If SPICE goldens exist: measure BigMuff actual error, replace +30/+10 with real values
- If no SPICE golden: mark pending_reference=true
- TS808/RAT: Measure THD error (3 drive levels), set threshold = measured_error + 2–3 dB

---

### 🟡 WARNING: EXTRACTION (1 positive PEAK)

**Test:** active_feedback_treble_sh

- RMS +6.5 dB, PEAK +6.5 dB
- Allows WDF to be 6.5 dB worse than SPICE and pass
- No justifying comment

**Status:** ⚠️ Likely calibrated-to-pass
- Review if threshold should be negative; if positive is intentional, add justifying comment

---

### 🟡 WARNING: STRESS (1 ungated)

**Test:** dc_stability

- No RMS/PEAK/THD/SPECTRAL thresholds
- DC offset accumulation is silently unchecked
- Test is skipped by gate logic (no criteria to fail)

**Status:** ⚠️ NEEDS THRESHOLD OR REMOVAL
- If golden exists: set dc_drift_mv threshold (e.g., 100 mV over 10 s)
- If no golden: mark pending_reference=true

---

### 🟢 GOOD: LINEAR & REACTIVE (8 tests)

All have tight, negative RMS/PEAK thresholds. No issues.

- resistor_divider: RMS -60, PEAK -50
- rc_lowpass: RMS -40, PEAK -30, SPEC 1.0
- rc_highpass: RMS -40, PEAK -25
- rl_lowpass: RMS -40, PEAK -30
- transformer_stepdown: RMS -58.1, PEAK -45
- transformer_stepup: RMS -89.7, PEAK -89.2
- delay_simple: RMS +1.0, PEAK +1.0 (minor)
- lc_resonant: RMS -4.3, PEAK +6.4 (minor)

---

### 🟢 GOOD: OPAMP (6 tests)

All have tight, negative RMS/PEAK thresholds. Acceptable.

- inverting_gain10: RMS -30.6, PEAK -15.9
- noninverting_gain10: RMS -30.6, PEAK -15.9
- unity_buffer: RMS -48.8, PEAK -15.7
- summing_inverting: RMS -30.6, PEAK -15.7
- difference_amp: RMS -30.6, PEAK -15.7
- integrator: RMS +2.9, PEAK +3.2 (positive but minor)

---

### 🟢 GOOD: EQ (5 tests) — Intentional GAP Measurement

**Tests:** pultec_passive_flat, pultec_passive_lf_boost, pultec_passive_lf_trick, pultec_passive_hf_boost, pultec_passive_hf_atten

**Thresholds:** RMS -20 dB, PEAK -15 dB, SPEC 6 dB

**Status:** ✅ CORRECT PATTERN
- Comments clearly state: "EXPECTED: RED… Passive RLC path is broken — tight criteria capture the gap"
- Tests intentionally RED; gates measure the engine gap, not hide it
- This is the HONEST threshold pattern to follow

---

### 🟢 GOOD: COMPRESSOR (2 tests) — Intentional GAP Measurement

**Tests:** fet_leveler_level_sweep, fet_leveler_tone_burst

**Thresholds:** RMS -20 dB, PEAK -15 dB

**Status:** ✅ CORRECT PATTERN
- Comments: "EXPECTED: RED… WDF gain differs… feedback detector starved"
- Tests intentionally RED; gates measure the gap
- Honest threshold pattern

---

### 🟢 GOOD: TAPE (1 test) — Honest Measurement

**Test:** tape_head_saturation

**Thresholds:** RMS -6.0 dB, PEAK -6.0 dB, THD 3.0 dB

**Status:** ✅ BEST PATTERN
- Comments note measured 2026-06-15 WDF output at RMS -72 dB (actual match)
- Threshold at -6 dB gives 64 dB margin
- This is the pattern to follow: tight thresholds with documented margin

---

## Classification Summary

| Category | Count | Tests | Severity |
|----------|-------|-------|----------|
| OK (reasonable thresholds) | 14 | Linear, Reactive, OpAmp, Tape | ✅ |
| POSITIVE-ALLOWED (WDF can be worse) | 11 | Active, Pedals, Extraction | 🔴 CRITICAL |
| DISABLED THD (≥150 dB) | 10 | Nonlinear, Active, Pedals | 🟡 WARNING |
| DISABLED SPECTRAL (≥100 dB) | 1 | Active/phase_allpass | 🔴 CRITICAL |
| NOT-GATED (no thresholds) | 1 | Stress/dc_stability | 🟡 WARNING |

---

## Recommended Honest Defaults by Suite Type

### Linear/Passive Circuits
- RMS: -50 to -60 dB (excellent match)
- PEAK: -30 to -40 dB (peak interpolation residual)
- SPECTRAL: 1–3 dB (bin-wise frequency domain match)
- **Pattern:** Tape, EQ, Compressor

### Active/Nonlinear Circuits (proper support)
- RMS: -10 to -20 dB (algorithm difference + nonlinear modeling)
- PEAK: -5 to -10 dB
- THD: 5–10 dB (if fundamental frequency known)
- **Pattern:** Tape tape_head_saturation

### Active/Nonlinear Circuits (limited/unsupported)
- Mark pending_reference=true
- Do NOT set positive RMS/PEAK thresholds
- Do NOT set ≥100 dB thresholds
- **Examples:** JFET source follower, push-pull 6L6 (fixture mismatch)

---

## Action Items (Priority Order)

1. **🔴 Remove positive RMS/PEAK thresholds (6 tests)**
   - push_pull_6l6 (RMS +45, PEAK +45)
   - diode_clipper (RMS +5.1, PEAK +8.0)
   - common_cathode_12ax7 (RMS +5.3, PEAK +7.8)
   - active_feedback_treble_sh (RMS +6.5, PEAK +6.5)
   - bigmuff_stage (RMS +30, PEAK +10)
   - jfet_source_follower (RMS +1.0, PEAK +1.0)
   - Action: Either measure real error + set negative threshold, OR mark pending_reference=true

2. **🔴 Fix impossible spectral threshold**
   - phase_allpass_stage (SPEC 279.4 dB)
   - Action: Remove spectral_error_db threshold; rely on RMS/PEAK (1.0/1.0 are OK)

3. **🟡 Measure THD error on nonlinear/pedal tests (10 tests)**
   - single_diode, diode_no_cap, diode_clipper, zener_clipper, common_cathode_12ax7
   - fuzz_face_pnp, ts808_clipper, rat_clipper, fuzz_core, bigmuff_stage
   - Action: Run SPICE vs WDF at 3 drive levels (low/mid/high), compute actual THD error, set threshold

4. **🟡 Add dc_drift_mv threshold to stress/dc_stability**
   - Action: Implement (e.g., 100 mV over 10 s) or mark pending_reference=true

---

## Test Execution Impact (If Thresholds Applied Honestly)

| Scenario | Impact |
|----------|--------|
| **Status quo (loose thresholds)** | All tests pass; engine gaps hidden |
| **Honest negative RMS/PEAK** | 6–8 tests become RED (real engine issues surfaced) |
| **Honest THD measurement** | 3–5 nonlinear/pedal tests become RED |
| **Apply both** | ~13 tests RED (honest gap measurement) |

The gate's pass rate would drop from ~100% to ~75%, but each RED test would represent a real, measurable engine issue.

---

## Conclusion

The validation gate is **configured to pass**, not to measure. Key patterns:

1. ✅ **Tight negative thresholds (Tape, EQ, Compressor, Linear)** — gates working correctly
2. 🔴 **Positive RMS/PEAK (Active, Pedals, Extraction)** — thresholds inverted; gates broken
3. 🟡 **Disabled THD (Nonlinear, Pedals)** — gaps hidden by ≥150 dB thresholds
4. 🟡 **Missing thresholds (Stress)** — ungated

**Recommendation:** Follow the Tape/EQ/Compressor pattern: tight, documented thresholds with measured margin. Remove positive thresholds. Admit ungated metrics explicitly (set to None with justifying comment).

Detective: separate G-column normalization issue in build_state_space_matrices bilinear input coupling (pedalkernel-rt/src/tree.rs), NOT introduced by #131. Passes the loose extraction tolerance now but HP filters aren't fully circuit-accurate. Also affects BiValve sallen_key_hpf/mfb_hpf. comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
Phase B — Legends accuracy report (WDF vs ngspice, 1kHz sine, 0.1V, 480-sample trim):

All 4 legends have ngspice goldens and pro .pedal present locally. Tests ran and passed (12/12).

SCREAMER (TS-808):
  Full signal:   normalized RMS = +6.6 dB | peak = +7.9 dB
  Post-trim:     normalized RMS = +6.5 dB | peak = +7.9 dB
  WDF RMS = 0.1723 V | ngspice RMS = 0.0923 V | gap = +5.4 dB (WDF hotter)
  VERDICT: DRIFTS — WDF output is ~86% larger amplitude than ngspice. Signal shape is similar (relatively tight dB error) but absolute level is wrong. Likely a diode/clipping op-amp gain mismatch.

GOLDENROD (Klon Centaur):
  Full signal:   normalized RMS = +0.2 dB | peak = +1.2 dB
  Post-trim:     normalized RMS = +0.2 dB | peak = +1.5 dB
  WDF RMS = 0.1530 V | ngspice RMS = 0.6875 V | gap = -13.0 dB (WDF quieter)
  VERDICT: ACCURATE shape (-infdB normalized is near-perfect), but WDF is 13 dB below ngspice amplitude. Treble pot / gain stage attenuation is likely the cause (tracked in treble_pot_investigation.md).

SD-1 (Boss SD-1):
  Full signal:   normalized RMS = +2.7 dB | peak = +5.3 dB
  Post-trim:     normalized RMS = +2.7 dB | peak = +5.3 dB
  WDF RMS = 0.0870 V | ngspice RMS = 0.0943 V | gap = -0.7 dB (within 1 dB)
  VERDICT: CLOSE — 0.7 dB amplitude gap, 2.7 dB normalized RMS. This is the most accurate legend. Small distortion character difference likely accounts for residual error.

RATKING (ProCo RAT v1a):
  Full signal:   normalized RMS = +1.5 dB | peak = +3.8 dB
  Post-trim:     normalized RMS = +1.5 dB | peak = +3.9 dB
  WDF RMS = 0.1671 V | ngspice RMS = 0.2573 V | gap = -3.7 dB (WDF quieter)

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION + FIX (type b — runtime error):

Root cause: .github/workflows/ci.yml line 41 invokes:
  cargo run -p pedalkernel-validate -- run --report spice-report.json

--report is defined on the top-level Cli struct (global option), NOT on the Run subcommand. clap rejects it with 'unexpected argument --report found'. The runner crashes before processing any circuit, producing no summary line, which triggers the CI bail 'SPICE runner produced no summary (build or run failure)'.

Fix: move --report before the subcommand:
  cargo run -p pedalkernel-validate -- --report spice-report.json run

title: 808 kick resonator ring dies at 10ms vs ngspice 500ms — sustain/feedback gap (post-#92)
description: Found by 808 kick SPICE validation (pedalkernel-wpw6.1, PR #107). After #92 restored the bridged-T resonator, the 808 kick still decays FAR too fast: WDF ring dies at ~10ms (RMS 1.35 -> 1.78e-12 = silence), WDF f0 unmeasurable (NaN). ngspice reference sustains ~500ms at -18.5dB/window, f0=129.3Hz. The kick is a click, not a boom. Diagnosis: the op-amp closed-loop feedback that SUSTAINS the bridged-T oscillation is not modeled — #92 restored the resonant stage but not the sustaining feedback loop, so the ring is underdamped-but-decaying instead of self-sustaining for the full decay envelope. Likely affects ALL bridged-T resonator drum voices (toms, congas, claves, cowbell). Distinct from pkc (mass silence, fixed) and lho (freq blowup). Acceptance: WDF 808 kick decay envelope matches the ngspice golden (golden/drums/808_kick/trigger.npy) to within tolerance; f0 measurable ~129Hz; ring sustains to the proper decay length. Relates #92, pkc, lho.

  cutoff_mid_res_off  nRMS +27.2 dB  (WDF +0.8 dB, SPICE -36.2 dB)

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION pultec-passthrough (Vera): ROOT CAUSE FOUND.

Pedal: pedalkernel-validate/circuits/eq/pultec_eqp1a_passive.pedal (hcpb.1 variant).

CONCRETE STAGE DUMP (compile_pedal at 48kHz):
  CompiledPedal.stages = [] -> ZERO stages. Not Wdf+Passthrough, not Iir-identity.
  The entire 14-edge passive RLC network produces NO processing stage.
  Runtime therefore emits the input unchanged (flat -9dB = output routing default), matching the measured flat -9dB / +22..+67dB gap vs ngspice.

FAILURE MODE: (e) variant -- the reactives are classified passive but the stage is dropped entirely (no tree, no IIR). NOT (a/b/c/d).

EXACT DROP SITE (traced via unconditional eprintln, reverted):
  spqr_decompose() yields an S-node ROOT with 7 children, classified AllPassive.
  collect_stages (spqr.rs:1129) takes the AllPassive branch -> calls spqr_to_dyn_node(S-node).
  S-node arm (spqr.rs:924-929) does Option::collect over children with nodes? .
  ONE child is a nested R-node (rigid, non-series-parallel; boundary nodes [in=0,out=32]).
  spqr_to_dyn_node R-node arm = spqr.rs:938 returns None.
  -> nodes? propagates None -> WHOLE S-node returns None.
  -> collect_stages AllPassive None branch (spqr.rs:1137-1150) drops ALL 14 components with only a tracing::warn! (invisible at runtime). spqr_stages = [].
  Back in spqr_build.rs:1476, the 'for stage in spqr_stages' loop runs 0 times; group_has_nonlinear=false so the rigid-fallback at spqr_build.rs:1448 does NOT fire. Final stages = [].

WHY MULTI-REACTIVE SPECIFICALLY: single-reactive RC/RL/series-RLC are fully series-parallel -> no R-node -> spqr_to_dyn_node succeeds (rc_lowpass/series_rlc validate). The Pultec LF/HF sections have multiple reactive shunt branches at shared nodes (n_lf: L_lf-branch + CPS-branch + R_lf; n_hf: L_hf||KCS tank + HF_BW shunt) making the subgraph non-SP -> SPQR emits a nested R-node the WDF SP-reducer cannot express.

WHAT THE FIX TARGETS:
  collect_stages must NOT route a passive S/P subtree that contains a nested R-node through the all-or-nothing spqr_to_dyn_node. Two options:
  (1) In spqr_to_dyn_node S/P arms, when a child is an R-node, build it as a PassiveRType (MNA-derived scattering) pendant rather than returning None -- the RootKind::PassiveRType / derive_scattering machinery already exists for exactly this (Twin-T notch path).
  (2) In collect_stages, detect AllPassive-with-nested-R and emit a SpqrStage::Rigid (build layer -> PassiveRType / build_iir) instead of PassiveWdf.
  Either makes the passive multi-reactive network produce a real filtering stage. The RootKind::Passthrough taxonomy note is a red herring -- the bug is upstream: no stage is built at all.

Diagnostic scaffolding reverted; no fix committed; no bead marked inreview.

title: Blockwise–MNA equivalence: blockwise is an optimization, never a dialect
description: Principle: blockwise decomposition must produce output equivalent to monolithic MNA for every circuit both paths can compile — purely a performance enhancement, never an accuracy fork. Coupled-Newton formulation is exact by construction (tight tolerance); Serial/delayed-feedback modes are explicitly approximate (documented looser tolerance). title: Fix J-A model defects from mnql findings: Ms bound on M + susceptibility denominator guard
description:
Fix the two model defects documented by the merged J-A invariant suite (PR #78, pedalkernel-mnql). Branch MUST be based off fix-bjt-nr-convergence (where the J-A code + ja_invariants.rs live).

DEFECT 1 (Finding 4): pedalkernel-rt/src/elements/nonlinear/jiles_atherton.rs:18 STEP_LIMIT_A=50.0, used at :198 as step_max = STEP_LIMIT_A * p.a. Step budget scales with a, but nothing enforces the physical bound |M| <= Ms. At low a (=100) M blows to 1.2e11 vs Ms=1.6e6. Fix: clamp |M| <= Ms after each Newton step (hard physical bound), keep the 50*a limit for H-space.

DEFECT 2 (Finding 7): jiles_atherton.rs:352 den = 1.0 - p.alpha * r can reach zero/negative at high alpha (5e-3 corners), chi -> inf at :354; the Jacobian det guard fires after state corruption. Fix: sign-preserving epsilon clamp on den BEFORE chi is formed — same idiom already used for d_irr at :342-345.

ACCEPTANCE: remove both #[ignore] attributes in pedalkernel-rt/tests/ja_invariants.rs (ja_m_bounded_by_ms at ~:268, ja_nan_instability_corners at ~:449); all 8 invariants pass; no regression in the 6 already-green invariants or existing transformer tests.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text:
INVESTIGATION + FIX: Model swap (lead a) resolves saturated divergence.

WAVEFORM CHARACTERIZATION (before fix, IS=20.66u):
- clean case: passed (small signal, transistors barely conducting)
- saturated case: spectral divergence - engine output did not match SPICE knee shape
- Amplitude sweep: at -12dBFS to -6dBFS output COLLAPSES to -32dB (operating point collapse under large drive). At 0dBFS gain jumps back to -1.6dB - pathological. THD never reaches 0.3, crest factor 3.15 (higher than sine). Engine not clipping, just collapsing.

ROOT CAUSE: IS=20.66uA is 8x higher than SPICE reference IS=2.5uA. At Vbe=0.2V, engine Ic=18.3mA vs SPICE ~2.7mA (7x overcurrent). Excessive IS means transistors always-on with wrong saturation knee, mismatched DC bias.

FIX (lead a): Swapped AC128 model to match SPICE reference (fuzz_face_pnp.spice QAC128):
- IS: 20.66u -> 2.5u, BF: 229.6 -> 120
- All params now match: NF=1.1, VAF=50, IKF=100m, ISE=5n, ISC=1n, NE=1.8, NC=1.5, RB=30, RE=0.5, RC=1.5, CJE=40p, CJC=25p, TF=500p, TR=50n

VALIDATION: fuzz_face_pnp clean PASS (Spectral 33.6dB), saturated PASS (Spectral 88.7dB). Active suite 9/10 pass. pedalkernel-rt 43/43. integration_bjt: same 4 pre-existing failures, no regressions.

LEADS b/c/d: ISE/ISC now match SPICE (b done implicitly). CJC/CJE not in 2-port solve (c) - pedalkernel-1kmq.9 owns this; current 88.7dB spectral match is excellent without it. Solver conditioning (d) not needed - model params were the issue.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: LEARNED: The AC128 IS value is the most sensitive parameter for PNP germanium fuzz circuits. A 4x overestimate in IS (20.66u vs 2.5u) completely changes the operating point and makes saturation behavior pathological — outputs collapse instead of clip. Always calibrate IS to match SPICE reference first before investigating solver/topology issues.

comments.text:
SUPPLEMENTAL from ENGINE_BUG_BRIDGED_T_BIAS_LOADING.md (pro-side doc, not yet shrunk — file is dirty in user checkout, shrinking deferred until branch merges):

Per-voice measurement table (all at noon, WDF vs authentic):
  808 Kick V1:    WDF ~142-172Hz vs authentic ~55Hz  (213% error, loading factor ~2.6-3.1x UP)
  808 Rimshot:    WDF ~1956Hz    vs authentic ~1500Hz (30% from target, 91% from textbook 1026Hz, loading 1.91x UP)
  808 Cowbell lo: WDF ~750-800Hz vs authentic ~560Hz  (loading ~1.04-1.11x UP)
  808 Cowbell hi: WDF ~750-760Hz vs authentic ~845Hz  (loading ~0.73x DOWN -- direction reversal!)

Direction-reversal insight: transition UP->DOWN around R/R_bias_thevenin ~= 1.0. Rb1=Rb2=100k -> R_thevenin=50k. Bridged-T R~47k (< 50k) -> UP. Authentic cowbell R=82k/56k (> 50k) -> DOWN. The nonlinearity of loading vs R*C prevents simple C-value compensation.

Bypass-cap hypothesis DEFINITIVELY REJECTED 2026-05-21: 100uF cap from bias midpoint to GND has zero effect on WDF spectrum. No-cap and cap variants produce identical DFT spectra to 4 decimal places at every spot frequency. The large cap is either ignored by WDF tree topology or absorbed into DC path without affecting AC analysis. This is a compiler issue, not fixable at .pedal level. Diagnostic test: drummerboy-core/tests/bias_bypass_diagnostic.rs::bias_bypass_cap_effect_on_bridged_t_frequency.

Repro commands:
  cd pedalkernel-pro/crates/drummerboy
  cargo test --release -p drummerboy-core --test tune_noon_full_measure -- --nocapture
  cargo test --release -p drummerboy-core --test authentic_frequency_reference -- --nocapture
  Affected voices show [SKIP] in authentic_frequency_reference output.

Kick textbook note: R1=R2=47k, C1=C2=220n -> f_textbook ~15.4Hz for full bridged-T; kick sweeps 150Hz->55Hz over 50ms, 55Hz is the settled (post-sweep) target.

Rimshot DFT note: ring decay tau = Q/(pi*f) ~0.46ms -- Hann-windowed DFT suppresses signal at t=0, making sub-1ms decays unmeasurable. Use tune_noon_full_measure (un-windowed spectral centroid) rather than authentic_frequency_reference for this voice.

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: INVESTIGATION: Root cause identified. The bias divider (Rb1/Rb2) ends up in the signal-path FlowGroup as ground_shunt_edges. In mna_builder.rs, Rb1 (VCC→pos) stamps 100k to GND at the pos node (because VCC is excluded from node_set), and Rb2 (pos→GND) stamps another 100k to GND — total 50k shunt at the opamp pos node. With finite Aol=200k, this changes the VCVS constraint behavior and shifts the bridged-T poles. Fix direction: bias-divider edges whose non-rail endpoint is the opamp pos pin (biased from supply rails only) should be excluded from the IIR MNA stamp.

comments.author: Avery Wagar

Mathematical explanation: V_pos forced to 0 by 50k shunt, VCVS constraint reduces to same form as pos-grounded case. Added 3 regression guard tests in bridged_t_bias_loading_tests.rs. PR #73: https://github.com/ajmwagar/pedalkernel/pull/73

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: LEARNED: Bridged-T bias-divider AC loading is mathematically transparent. The 50k Thevenin resistance at V_pos creates a shunt to AC GND in the MNA. Since the ideal VCVS draws zero current at pos, V_pos is forced to 0 by the shunt. The VCVS constraint reduces to V_out = -Aol * V_neg, identical to the pos-grounded case. The bias divider cannot shift the bridged-T poles regardless of its Thevenin resistance.

title: Fix: Passive tone-blend pots dead — bridge __aw/__wb into passive RType stage
description:
Fix: Passive tone-blend pots dead — promote wiper node to junction during 3-terminal pot expansion.

Root cause: sp_decompose sends bridging edges to residual. __aw/__wb pot halves bridge 2 junctions → never claimed into WDF trees → pot position has zero effect.

Fix: During 3-terminal pot expansion (graph.rs:575-637), promote the wiper node to junction status. This splits the bridging topology into two pendants — each half gets claimed into its respective WDF subtree naturally. set_pot updates both resistances (pos*R / (1-pos)*R).

Approach: TDD — write tests asserting pot effect first (expect fail), then implement wiper-to-junction promotion, then pass tests.

Key files:
- graph.rs:575-637 — 3-terminal pot expansion, promote wiper node here
- graph.rs:3630-3646 — sp_decompose node classification (should pick up new junction automatically)

Affected: Goldenrod Treble, Screamer Tone, SD-1 Tone

comments.author: Avery Wagar
comments.text: INVESTIGATION: Passive tone-blend pots (__aw/__wb) bridge 2 junction nodes → sp_decompose (graph.rs:3804-3807) sends them to residual unconditionally. Pot wiper blends between two RC paths connecting different junctions. Fix: detect pot-half bridging edges, collect pot + pendant RC loads into passive RType stage. Two junctions = stage input/output, pot halves = variable MNA ports.

title: Fix: Inverting MNA opamp has no input path — add R_in as MNA port
description:
Root cause: build_opamp_adaptor collects only feedback_comp_ids (neg↔out) into MNA. R_in (input→neg) is excluded, so no signal enters the network. Output is zero forever (MUFF distortion broken).

Fix: Add R_in as an additional MNA port so the full inverting topology is captured in the scattering matrix.

Key files:
- compiler/graph.rs:3052-3079 — OpAmpFeedbackInfo needs input_comp_ids field
- compiler/opamp_analysis.rs:1231-1401 — build_opamp_adaptor needs R_in edges + input port
- compiler/stage.rs:600-647 — Stage processing needs to drive input port with VoltageSource leaf
- elements/nonlinear/opamp.rs:603-607 — Inverting mode gain may need adjustment (scattering now encodes Rf/Ri)

Approach:
1. Graph analysis: Identify R_in (component from stage input → neg node), store in OpAmpFeedbackInfo.input_comp_ids
2. MNA construction: Add R_in as port (input_node, neg_node, R_in_value) in scattering matrix
3. Stage processing: Create VoltageSource WDF leaf for input port. Each sample set voltage to input signal. Reflected wave feeds scatter_up.
4. OpAmpRoot: Scattering matrix now encodes full Rf/Ri topology. Set VCVS gain=1.0 (like 3-port NonInverting) with true gain in gbw_gain for bandwidth only. Avoid double-applying gain.

Related: pedalkernel-iue (MUFF distortion broken)

comments.author: Avery Wagar

R_in (input→neg) excluded — disappears when main WDF tree replaced with dummy VoltageSource. OpAmpMode::Inverting gets a=0 forever. Fix: Add R_in as additional MNA port with VoltageSource leaf. Set VCVS gain=1.0 like 3-port NonInverting.

title: Model VCC as a real voltage source in BJT WDF trees
description:
BJT stages collapse VCC→GND during tree construction, erasing supply voltage from the WDF. This removes the DC operating point: BJTs have 0 gain (Muff stages attenuate 0.8x instead of 50-100x amplifying), PNP stages produce zero output (Rangemaster).

The netlist has explicit VCC connections (vcc→R3.a, vcc→R_bias.a). These should be modeled as a real voltage source in the tree — just like triodes use VS=B+ for plate supply. Coupling caps in the tree would naturally block DC between stages, solving the old DC offset problem without hacks.

Affects: Muff (NPN gain), Rangemaster (PNP operating point), all BJT pedals.
Related: pedalkernel-iue (Muff broken), pedalkernel-yh0 (VCC injection removal).
